items.Invariants / obligations: A delta requires an actual sediment-fed mouth and compatible coastal accommodation space; no delta where the material was exported or the ocean boundary is cropped away. Interpret real accumulated materials rather than drawing depositional land from a classification field.
items.Review notes: The semantic 'formation' is physically owned by river-mouth and coastal sediment mechanisms; this roster entry should recognize that result, not double-count material. Leave a separate progradation/avulsion mechanism as a future design question.

items.Semantic name: Ocean proximity and continentality context
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Compute how far land and water locations lie from the ocean, providing continentality context for other processes.
items.Observable effects: Places can be interpreted as ocean-facing, maritime, coastal or far inland; downstream climate and ecological patterns vary with true exposure to marine water. This calculation does not create new landforms, seas or climatic processes.
items.Fields & products read: Current connected-ocean mask and shoreline location, cell distances/geographic metric, optional parent/neighbor distance-to-ocean field and the open-ocean boundary beyond a cropped map.
items.Fields & products written: Derived OceanDistance and associated maritime/continentality context for other process owners; no change to water, rock, ice or material history.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Supplies ocean-distance context to air-temperature moderation, moisture transport, warmth sources and other users that need maritime access. A clipped land-only child obtains actual distance through a captured boundary provider, not by inferring that there is no nearby sea.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: Present-state spatial query at any map type/resolution where continentality matters; recompute when coastline changes, without elapsed years or local sea creation. Long-distance context may come from a coarser parent rather than being solved within a Street map.
items.Other process interactions: Receives marine shoreline from ocean connectivity and coastal evolution. Feeds atmospheric and habitat interpretation, coastal site opportunities, seaward transport and the distinction between inland and ocean-influenced landscapes.
items.Invariants / obligations: Distance is measured to connected marine water, not an arbitrary freshwater lake or a child-map boundary. Land-only crops must not become infinitely continental; preserve units and distinguish unknown external context from confirmed absence of an ocean.
items.Review notes: Derived context, not an ocean-forming process. Its sole contract is to answer maritime proximity consistently across independently bounded maps.

items.Semantic name: Seafloor depth and bathymetric-zone classification
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Classify submerged relief and bathymetric zones from water depth and seafloor slope.
items.Observable effects: Existing seafloor resolves into shallow shelves, shelf breaks, slopes and deep basins, with coastal shallows and steep underwater ground available as meaningful geographic context. Classification makes seabed structure legible; it does not carve that structure.
items.Fields & products read: Present connected marine-water occupancy and sea stand, retained seabed elevation, standing-water depth, slope and shelf-break significance thresholds; inherited offshore context where the local map does not encompass the whole shelf.
items.Fields & products written: Derived bathymetric zone classes and slope/depth interpretation for geography, currents, ecology, navigation and map publication. Does not create crust, alter sea level or deposit sediment.
items.Shared questions / coupling: A classification contract on the shared seabed/water columns supplies shelf/deep-water status to circulation, Pressure propagation, marine habitats and geographically significant sea/shore features. Numerical water depth remains independent of the displayed zone label.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: Present interpretation at World and coastal Region/City/Street scales as supported by actual cell resolution; read boundary bathymetry for truncated offshore surroundings. Not a geological epoch or a bathymetric sculpting process.
items.Other process interactions: The classifier reads submarine tectonics, marine sedimentation, erosion, sea-level change and ocean connectivity. Its derived classes help identify shelf-associated currents, fisheries, oceanic crossings and named maritime regions.
items.Invariants / obligations: Shelf, slope and deep-water categories follow actual sea depth and seafloor morphology; a label may not imply material that was never generated. Lakes are not automatically oceanic shelves. Inherited named underwater places retain identity independently of class thresholds.
items.Review notes: Classification / derived geography; the old 'realization/publication' label was too broad. Publication can draw the categories, but this contract interprets existing numerical seabed and marine state.

items.Semantic name: Emergent landmass and continental-shelf grouping
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Identify connected landmasses, their classes, and groups joined through continental shelves.
items.Observable effects: Islands, larger landmasses and island chains resting on a shared shallow shelf are recognized as distinct yet related geographic formations. Their mapped relationships expose useful island/continental geography without constructing new crust or flooding water.
items.Fields & products read: Connected dry-land masks and current shore geometry; retained elevations, water occupancy, sea stand, submerged shelf-break relief and the broader parent/adjacent footprint; established landmass identities and geographically significant names.
items.Fields & products written: Derived connected landmass IDs, size/significance classes and shelf-connected group IDs; relationships for geographic recognition/publication by the relevant place/catalogue owner. Does not move plates or add land.
items.Shared questions / coupling: A current-topology and scale-dependent grouping contract. Ocean connectivity defines exposed islands and seas; bathymetric shelf depth groups emergent masses; naming/significance rules and identity inheritance keep catalog entities stable.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: Present landmass/shelf classification on World and finer maps. Region, City and Street crops inherit landmass membership and external coast/shelf connectivity rather than becoming new islands or continental groups because of the selected outline.
items.Other process interactions: Tectonic history, volcanic island formation, ice/sea-level change, erosion and deposition establish physical shapes; biogeography, current barriers, maritime transport and political/cultural reach can read the emergent groupings.
items.Invariants / obligations: Distinguish exposed land adjacency from underwater shelf connection and both from tectonic ancestry. A cropped map edge is not a new coast; a continental shelf relationship is not necessarily one plate. Named landmass identities persist where the finer geometry remains within them.
items.Review notes: Derived geography/grouping, not continental construction or GIS publication itself. It computes present land/shelf relationships; separate geographic significance and publication decide which groups are named and drawn.

items.Semantic name: Ocean circulation, heat transport and wave exposure
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Develop ocean-current directions and strengths, together with associated wave exposure, from marine geography.
items.Observable effects: Large and regional gyres, swift coasts, still sheltered waters, warm wakes and cold/upwelling fronts arise from ocean geography. They produce exposed versus sheltered shores, fog/fisheries differences, transported warmth and storm-prone sea-air boundaries.
items.Fields & products read: Connected sea geometry, bathymetric depth/shelf obstacles and straits, latitude and climate/wind forcing, incoming or inherited current/heat at open marine boundaries, geothermal and other marine heat sources, wave fetch, plus Pressure or other system-specific ocean forcing.
items.Fields & products written: Ocean current vectors and strengths, heat advection/sea-surface anomalies, upwelling and fetch-driven wave-exposure products, coastal thermal forcing and circulation context retained for atmosphere, ecology and erosion.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Physical marine circulation responds to sea connectivity, basin geometry, atmosphere and energy sources through shared current/heat/wave answers. Pressure may superpose distinct deep-water rays, wakes and storm forcing; do not collapse those effects into a generic magic or temperature scalar.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: World-scale and regional ocean circulation is physically coupled to broad connected basins; nearshore Region/City/Street refinement receives consistent external offshore transport/heat/wave context and may resolve local fronts without recomputing a new disconnected global gyre.
items.Other process interactions: Sea level and changing straits redirect currents; geothermal heat and Pressure alter marine fronts, which affect storms, fog, fisheries, glaciation/sea ice, coastal abrasion and sediment dispersal. Hallowed boundaries can influence supported magic/storm interactions independently.
items.Invariants / obligations: Flow follows connected water and physical marine barriers; cannot cross dry land or arise solely because a clipped local map omits its source. Maintain coherent upstream heat/energy forcing and differentiate currents, fetch/waves and Pressure's physical medium. No arbitrary 'warm coast' label without ocean process.
items.Review notes: Canonical physical circulation phenomenon; sea-surface anomalies, thermal transport and wave exposure are coupled consequences, not automatically separate independent processes. Child strategies consume the source ocean as a boundary condition.

items.Semantic name: Localized thermal and geothermal forcing context
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Distribute localized and ocean-influenced warmth sources that contribute to the temperature field.
items.Observable effects: Hot springs, warmed channels, warmer lee or ocean-influenced areas, cooled glacier fronts and thermally exceptional landscapes receive specific heat influences rather than a uniform temperature offset. Such sources can sustain microclimates and seasonally ice-free water.
items.Fields & products read: Retained geothermal flux, volcanic/fracture heat, ocean circulation and water warmth, terrain height and coast position, climate background, legitimate Fire/Aurora/Pressure and other physical/magic heat interactions, inherited thermal source context and upstream/offshore influences.
items.Fields & products written: Localized effective warmth/thermal forcing and reach/ground heat contributions available to atmospheric, river/groundwater, ice and ecology processes; source attribution and a derived warmth field. Does not manufacture new thermal material or independent climate epochs.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Heat-producing rock/magic/water owners retain the actual media and energy effects; this is a shared heat provider consumed by climate and water. Ocean currents transport ocean heat, atmospheric processes transport air heat; the provider does not replace either transport mechanism.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: Present forcing context across World and finer maps, with inherited physical sources and explicit heat flux or external ambient conditions; not another elapsed weather process. Narrow hot springs and cold gradients can be locally realized.
items.Other process interactions: Geothermal and magical sources inform atmosphere and river thermal regimes, ice melt/freeze and ecological zonation; shoreline and ocean currents transport the thermal consequences, settlements respond to usable warmth.
items.Invariants / obligations: Every anomaly needs a retained source or incoming heat boundary; avoid attributing energy to a named place without the corresponding medium. Heat fields must use consistent scale/units and must not be counted twice in climate and water processes.
items.Review notes: Derived thermal forcing/coupling contract, not an independently evolving atmosphere or a mechanism that creates volcanic activity.

items.Semantic name: Atmospheric circulation, moisture transport and precipitation
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Generate atmospheric temperature, winds, moisture transport, rainfall, snowfall, and storm patterns from geography and climate forcing.
items.Observable effects: Prevailing winds, rain shadows, seasonal storm tracks, maritime versus continental climates and snow zones arise from latitude, circulation and real terrain. Mountain faces, coasts and inland basins have distinct weather histories that affect water, ice, soil and habitation.
items.Fields & products read: Latitude/insolation and epoch climate forcing, height and orographic barriers, ocean temperature/currents and sea ice, local thermal/geothermal/magic sources, retained atmospheric moisture and wind context, active boundary air-mass inflow, previous climate state and temporal exposure.
items.Fields & products written: Temperature and seasonality, air demand, wind vectors/speed, upstream transport and moisture barriers, atmospheric moisture, storms, rain and snow supply, and explanatory climate histories where elapsed. Water, heat and moisture changes are sourced, transported and deposited coherently.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Shared climate/energy/water questions couple ocean heat, thermal anomalies, terrain, ecological evaporation and magical matter without bespoke POI cases. The hydrological owner receives rain/snow; it does not make the air move or generate new climate fields.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: Coupled atmosphere over a World through physical epochs; at Region/City/Street, boundary air and offshore context condition the present seasonal microclimate and local orographic detail without replaying ancestral centuries of precipitation.
items.Other process interactions: Feeds runoff, groundwater recharge, glaciers, ocean/wave regime, fires, ecological communities, weathering, population agriculture and travel. Sea and land surface feedback, magic and terrain changes can shift the climate across later epochs.
items.Invariants / obligations: Rain shadows and storms require meaningful upstream moisture/air sources; no isolated cropped-region climate that ignores the ocean beyond its boundary. Maintain physical seasonality and coherent snow/rain energy/water transfer, avoid unrelated noise overlays and preserve historic versus present time.
items.Review notes: Genuine coupled atmospheric phenomenon. May combine thermal, wind and moisture strategies internally, but their outputs arise from connected circulation and source exchange rather than three disconnected layer generators.

items.Semantic name: Precipitation, snow and soil-water partition into runoff
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Convert precipitation and snowmelt into surface runoff while accounting for snow, soil-water storage, and seasonal water movement.
items.Observable effects: Rainfall and seasonal thaw become visibly different perennial versus flash-flood watersheds: saturated valleys run, dry permeable slopes retain rain, snowmelt feeds seasonal creeks, and drought reduces surface supply without deleting stored groundwater.
items.Fields & products read: Rain and snow/snowpack through the year, temperature/seasonality, current soil-water and surface stores, slope/land cover, infiltration and evapotranspiration, meltwater/groundwater transfers, extracted/used water, inherited stores and external precipitation/snowmelt input.
items.Fields & products written: Updated snow, soil and shallow surface-water stocks, seasonal (e.g. monthly) surface-water availability, mean/dry/flood runoff, infiltration and withdrawal transfers in the common water ledger; time-stamped changes in stored water.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Atmospheric climate supplies precipitation; ecological soil and vegetation modify infiltration and interception; groundwater owns subsurface movement; glaciers own ice/snow release; hydrological water owners settle all transfers exactly once.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: Actual climate/seasonal water occurrence on World and relevant local developments; child Region/City/Street may recompute present seasonal distribution using inherited storage and true outside watershed supply, never rerun full ancestral climate periods.
items.Other process interactions: Feeds river-network discharge, lake filling, groundwater recharge, erosion and overbank flooding; deforestation, cultivation, magic altered weather and dams influence seasonal hydrological response.
items.Invariants / obligations: Water mass must be reconciled among precipitation, evaporation, infiltration, surface outflow, standing water and snow/soil stocks. Upstream discharge and retained snow/soil cannot vanish merely because the map footprint is small; avoid counting glacial melt twice.
items.Review notes: Distinct water-budget phenomenon; it produces supply and retained storage, not the choice of downstream path or the creation of a persistent channel.

items.Semantic name: Present river flow, seasonality and catchment context
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Resolve current river discharge, seasonal persistence and catchment measures as part of the established drainage and river-network system.
items.Observable effects: At any map's present moment, a named river has a coherent flow, perennial/ephemeral behavior, catchment and connected-channel attributes; local studies can recognize the same river even if most upstream source area is outside the view.
items.Fields & products read: Current routed runoff and upstream inflow, reach/routing graph, groundwater return, lake overflow or abstraction, wet/dry seasonal contributions, channel permeability, outside-basin boundary conditions and inherited river history.
items.Fields & products written: Derived current discharge, accumulated catchment area, flow/river-order and seasonal persistence readouts, seepage and reach-status context for hydraulics, navigation and ecological/social questions; no new channel incision or fresh river epoch.
items.Shared questions / coupling: The river-network owner exposes a read/refresh view from actual water inventory and retained reach identities. This provider does not rerun the elapsed channel-formation process; out-of-footprint headwater supply is an explicit input.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: On-demand present-state view on World, Region, City and Street at current resolution; re-evaluate when water inputs change. No elapsed river growth merely because a local map requests discharge.
items.Other process interactions: Used by channel geometry, floodplain and delta interpretation, sediment capacity, bridges/fords, fish habitat, wetlands, trade and settlement placement; updated after runoff, groundwater, lake releases, dams and aquifer interaction.
items.Invariants / obligations: Readouts must reflect the same water as the ledger and retained river network. Cropped maps may not silently recalculate the catchment solely from visible cells; querying unchanged state must not change river history or water volume.
items.Review notes: A supporting hydrological state provider within river-network ownership, not a second causal 'current-water' process.

items.Semantic name: Drainage outlet and depression topology preparation
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Condition terrain and drainage topology so the water-routing process can resolve connected flow.
items.Observable effects: Real drainage divides, low outlets and enclosed hollows are distinguishable even across flat ground; ambiguous flats receive coherent downstream connectivity so the later flow solution does not create imaginary lakes or cut channels.
items.Fields & products read: Current bed elevation/rock surface, mapped water/ocean/lake levels, true outlets and depression extents, inherited basin and downstream outlet links, parent slopes and outside-footprint boundary elevation/flow conditions.
items.Fields & products written: Derived conditioned water-routing surface, feasible outlet/depression connectivity and ordered drainage parent/rank context. This is computational routing context, not lifted/filled ground or deposited sediment.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Routing strategy supplies a topologically consistent context for actual flow selection. Lake basins own standing water; Ground/material owners change physical terrain when real floods, erosion or engineering modify it.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: Recompute as part of drainage-state realization when terrain or outlets change at any map type. Child conditioning must carry outside exits and incoming basin context; it is not historical terrain reshaping.
items.Other process interactions: Consumes coast and lake outlets, terrain and glacial/tectonic landforms; feeds flow routing and lake stage. Used after physical elevation changes and before accumulating watershed runoff.
items.Invariants / obligations: An abstract conditioned height must never be mistaken for actual terrain height. Do not inject sediment, invent lakes or close a river at the edge of a child; preserve connected basin paths and stable rerun results.
items.Review notes: Routing-state preparation within the drainage process's algorithm; it is not a separate erosion or deposition phenomenon.

items.Semantic name: Lake filling, surface stage and outlet exchange
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Identify and resolve lake basins, standing-water surfaces, lake outlets, and overflow under available water.
items.Observable effects: True depressions accumulate rain and incoming rivers into persistent lakes, shallow seasonal pools or intermittent closed-basin waters; overflow may create an outlet, recession exposes shores, and drying can leave saline material where supported.
items.Fields & products read: Real basin topography and depression connectivity, rainfall/runoff and river inflow, groundwater exchange, evapotranspiration and seepage, ice-water interactions, existing dams, stage/head and parent lake identity, outside-basin watershed supply.
items.Fields & products written: Lake-connected water bodies, retained volume/stage/depth and shoreline state, overflow and outlet discharge, seepage/evaporation/other water-ledger transfers and stable lake-basin relationships; actual bed/rock changes through separate sediment/material owners.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Shares water ledger with rivers, ocean, groundwater and runoff; use the same hydrostatic surface/head questions and material-backed basin relief. A lake's boundary provider accounts for upstream water and connections beyond the crop.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: Actual seasonal/epoch water storage on World; present lake extent, depth and outlet realization at Region/City/Street. Reuse inherited basins and water volumes instead of refilling an ancient reservoir from a cropped watershed.
items.Other process interactions: Runoff and aquifers fill lakes, rivers and channels drain their overflow, ice or dams obstruct outlets, drying changes ecology and can support salt mineral deposition; settlements depend on shores, potable water and crossings.
items.Invariants / obligations: Lake level, volume, evaporation, groundwater transfers and overflow must balance. Do not create inland water with no supported basin/inflow or erase a named lake because a child map sees only one bank; distinguish a marine bay from an isolated lake.
items.Review notes: Distinct standing-water storage and exchange phenomenon, not a terrain depression classifier alone. Retain the lake identity and stage while allowing detailed shore and outlet realization.

items.Semantic name: Topographic and inherited-channel routing guidance
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Provide terrain- and water-informed route preferences as a stage of the drainage and flow-routing process.
items.Observable effects: Across ambiguous slopes, the water graph favors real valleys, remembered established channels and passable drainage connections instead of producing discontinuous or arbitrary switchbacks between neighboring cells.
items.Fields & products read: Present conditioned drainage surface, true local gradients, existing river/channel evidence, physical bed and subsurface resistance, watershed/outlet context, inherited flow directions and external channel continuation.
items.Fields & products written: Derived admissible direction preferences and guidance targets for flow-routing decisions; it does not create water, change bed elevation or add channels by itself.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Acts as a replaceable routing strategy informed by ground, water and history, under the flow-routing semantic contract. Hydrological and geographic constraints outrank a purely aesthetic bias toward a preferred channel.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: Per-current-topography routing solve on World and children; guides finer paths consistently with parent outlets, named river courses and outside-footprint connectivity. Never an elapsed hydrological time step.
items.Other process interactions: Conditions flow routing and river continuity after glacial, tectonic, erosional or engineered changes; lake-basin spill choices and groundwater-related outlets can inform preferred exits.
items.Invariants / obligations: Guidance may influence only hydrologically admissible paths; preserve monotone/acyclic downstream flow as appropriate and distinguish temporary routing preference from physically cut bed channels.
items.Review notes: Non-process routing guidance/strategy, not a second independent 'drainage' simulation. Remains part of the flow-routing responsibility even if configured separately.

items.Semantic name: Connected drainage paths and watershed allocation
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Determine where water flows from each cell and assemble downstream flow links and drainage basins.
items.Observable effects: Water drains coherently from divides through joined tributaries to real lakes and the sea; nested catchments, endorheic basins, islands and crossing watersheds are recognizable, and rivers retain their identity across a selected map edge.
items.Fields & products read: Current terrain/conditioned slope, genuine outlets and shore/lake stages, drainage guidance and inherited river courses, permeability and distributed water supply, parent basin IDs and explicit outside-flow inlets/outlets.
items.Fields & products written: Directed flow targets/edges, basin/catchment membership and downstream route identity, route suitability and outlet connections for runoff aggregation. Does not itself consume water stocks or dig new channels.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Shared routing topology is consumed by runoff aggregation, sediment/water transport, river-network formation and groundwater return. Drainage conditioning and guidance are internal/derived strategies; only material owners sculpt terrain.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: On-demand present topology on World and finer maps after relevant terrain/water changes; children solve greater geometric detail with parent watershed and external boundary data without replaying past fluvial erosion.
items.Other process interactions: Interacts with lakes and outlet capture, tectonic elevation, glacial carving, sediment deposit, engineered dams, coastal sea level, erosion and standing-water networks; feeds river-discharge and floodplain interpreters.
items.Invariants / obligations: Flow graphs must have valid exits or explicitly closed basins and handle flats without unintended cycles; catchments cannot terminate at a crop boundary without an explicit transfer. No creation or loss of water/material by computing a path.
items.Review notes: Semantically one drainage-network responsibility; conditioning, guidance and path construction may be separate strategies, but should not each claim to be a distinct natural process.

items.Semantic name: River initiation, persistence and channel-network evolution
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Establish or evolve river channels and their network properties using routed runoff, catchments, and flow persistence.
items.Observable effects: Persistent discharge concentrates into streams of varying size and intermittence; tributaries join, headwater paths shift with erosion or capture, and named rivers carry coherent flow and history from highlands to mouths.
items.Fields & products read: Routed surface water and groundwater/baseflow, catchments and seasonal fluxes, actual terrain and bank/bed materials, flow-carrying capacity, retained channels and named river identities, lake outlets and upstream/outside river-network context.
items.Fields & products written: Retained river reaches, channel orders and connected courses, channel initiation/persistence or abandonment, catchment and discharge relationships, small-channel extent, evolving network history. Material excavation/deposition is delegated to fluvial processes.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Hydrological network owner integrates flow topology, water volumes and reach identity; the current-water provider computes derived readings without advancing the network. Geomorphic channels evolve through shared erosion/deposition and bank strength questions.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: World historical river-network formation under actual climate/terrain change; present Region/City/Street refinement resolves reaches and branches at higher fidelity from captured network and outside catchments, without recounting centuries of river growth.
items.Other process interactions: Receives drainage routing, runoff, lake/groundwater/dam and sea level; drives fluvial erosion, sediment transport, floodplain and delta interpretations, channel morphology, ecology, fisheries and settlement/travel.
items.Invariants / obligations: Named and hydrologically significant rivers must retain continuity across maps; a child cannot spawn or extinguish an established river due solely to cropping. Changes in course require a causal topographic/hydrologic reason, with matching channel/sediment and water budgets.
items.Review notes: Canonical river-network process; avoid confusing current derived river flow (`atlas.current-water`) with new network formation.

items.Semantic name: Coordinated ancestral denudation and river cutting
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Coordinate the coupled physical effects of stream incision, weathering, solution and slope creep on existing terrain.
items.Observable effects: A coherent history of weathered hillsides, incised valleys, dissolved soluble rock, degraded cliffs and redistributed colluvium emerges from jointly acting surface processes. The observable form is produced by those constituent mechanisms and their order—not by an independent 'ancestral erosion' force.
items.Fields & products read: Historical topography and rock columns; precipitation, runoff, stream network and outlet/base-level context; water chemistry and wetness, warmth/frost, fractures, root support, weathering mantle and previous erosion/deposition. Incoming river discharge and sediment at cut boundaries must be supplied explicitly.
items.Fields & products written: No unique physical field or material reservoir owned by the coordinator. It invokes weathering, incision, dissolution and creep/slope-transport owners, which write altered rock, removed material, routed cargo, channel floors and resulting historical landscape state under their own contracts.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Schedules shared questions for river flow, load/erosion capacity, wetness, climate, rock susceptibility and vegetative stabilization; participating processes act through ground modes and material routing, with the effects of earlier stages available to later stages.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: A World ancestral/historical geomorphic sequence under real epoch forcing and history, with optional scale-appropriate geomorphic composition during present Region/City/Street development. The latter refines current terrain from captured evidence without replaying ancient sediment or chemistry budgets.
items.Other process interactions: Coordinates weathering and solution with stream incision and gravity-driven creep; interacts with tectonic uplift, marine/coastal base levels, groundwater, ecology and downstream sediment transport. Each participating process can also be used independently at a different causal stage.
items.Invariants / obligations: The composite adds no separate erosion total on top of its participants, and must not reapply their effects when their outputs are read. Keep ordering explicit where undercutting, weathering, channel change and slope response alter one another; preserve materials and boundary flow through each participant.
items.Review notes: Orchestration/composition, not a catch-all semantic erosion process. Preserve independently meaningful weathering, fluvial incision, chemical solution and creeping transport as process contracts even when executed together.

items.Semantic name: Post-incision invocation of gravity-driven slope readjustment
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Redistribute unstable hillslope material after fluvial incision has altered the terrain.
items.Observable effects: Newly oversteepened valley walls retreat, collapsed material reaches the foot of cliffs and channel margins, and headwalls or fresh alluvial side slopes find a more supported profile after rivers cut them. These are manifestations of the ordinary mass-wasting mechanism.
items.Fields & products read: The *updated* rock surface and sediment/cover columns after fluvial incision and sediment routing; changed channel/valley geometry, slopes, root hold, water saturation and existing instability, plus all ordinary mass-wasting material and boundary inputs.
items.Fields & products written: No independent output ownership: the mass-wasting process moves retained rock and loose surface cargo to supported receiving areas, updating slope form, sediment packages and exposure just as it does in its earlier invocation.
items.Shared questions / coupling: A scheduling contract requires completed fluvial/chemical cuts and the same root-hold and material movement questions used by the canonical mass-wasting process. The changed geometric initial state is the meaningful distinction, not another type of landslide.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: A late geomorphic schedule position after river cutting in genuine World history, and after locally refined channels at Region/City/Street scales where necessary. It is not extra years of historical slope failure merely because another iteration ran.
items.Other process interactions: Takes results of stream incision and dissolving/weathering processes; redistributes their destabilized valley walls and supplies debris to subsequent sediment, soil, habitat and channel processes. It may be omitted if no new instability exists.
items.Invariants / obligations: Must reuse the mass-wasting identity, material ownership, source/destination obligations and stabilization logic. The same unsupported failure cannot be charged twice simply because two schedule points exist, and the post-incision call must observe the current terrain.
items.Review notes: Non-process scheduled occurrence/strategy of atlas.mass-wasting. Keep the ordering distinction in the execution plan, but do not count it as a second independent geological phenomenon.

items.Semantic name: Fluvial sediment routing, sorting and deposition
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Move available sediment through the river and drainage system according to transport capacity, including deposition along its course.
items.Observable effects: Active rivers carry eroded rock from uplands into gravel reaches, alluvial valley fills, floodplains, lake sediments, estuaries and deltas. Aggrading and sediment-starved reaches differ; material can bypass a reach or leave the modeled boundary rather than being forced to deposit locally.
items.Fields & products read: Real eroded/loose material cargo and grain or rock provenance; current routed discharge, channel geometry, gradient, flow and passage connectivity, sediment carrying capacity, lake/basin accommodation, sea-level/wave/current context and external incoming loads or outlets.
items.Fields & products written: Downstream transported load, material-composed deposits and retained sediments; modified channel/bed surfaces, floodplain or delta substrate, sediment supply for coastal/marine processes, and explicitly recorded outflow/load retained beyond the footprint.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Uses shared effective discharge, withdrawals, channel/routing and load-capacity questions; actual ground deposition and package routing through their owners. Hydrology owns where water flows, erosion owns liberated supply, and sediment transport owns its onward routing and settling.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: During World geomorphic history with actual water flow and sediment supply; spatially finer Region/City/Street strategies may resolve channel deposits or inherited sediment distribution under current conditions. Incoming and outgoing load across the selected area is an explicit boundary input/output, never silently zero.
items.Other process interactions: Receives weathering, river incision, mass-wasting, glaciers and human earthworks; routes sediment to lakes, deltas, marine systems and floodplains. Deposition alters slopes, channel bed levels, soil substrate, waterways and downstream flood and habitat patterns.
items.Invariants / obligations: No sediment created from discharge alone and no duplicate removal from source rock. Track material identity, volume at meaningful precision and receiving capacity; transported material cannot disappear at cropped edges, spill into unrelated basins or deposit on land unsupported by its routing.
items.Review notes: Distinct material-carrier process. Fluvial erosion creates supply and river dynamics supply flow; sediment transport owns the causal movement/deposition of that supply, including boundary exchange and river-to-sea handoff.

items.Semantic name: Sedimentary burial, consolidation and evaporite formation
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Consolidate buried loose sediment into rock and form evaporite deposits in suitable dry closed basins.
items.Observable effects: Older deposits harden into layered sedimentary stone, loose sediment becomes more resistant to weathering and erosion, and genuine evaporative basins leave salt or other evaporite beds. Later uplift and incision expose coherent strata, resistant ledges and former lakebeds.
items.Fields & products read: Retained loose sediment packages and material composition, burial depth/overburden, compaction history, water and pore conditions, relative geologic time, groundwater chemistry, basin closure, precipitation versus evaporation and existing organic or mineral inventories.
items.Fields & products written: Consolidated sedimentary rock layers with preserved origin and altered resistance/porosity, buried and remaining unconsolidated stocks, and authentic precipitated evaporite deposits in viable drying basins; updated rock/sediment layering for later deformation, metamorphism and erosion.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Rock-column and material-change contracts represent deposition, compaction, hardening and chemical precipitation without creating unbacked matter. Water/lake-balance and climate providers establish when evaporite precipitation is possible; organic-carbon burial uses the appropriate retained material pathways.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: A genuine geological burial/diagenesis process over elapsed World time, with occurrence at finer scales only for new physically caused deposition/burial. Region/City/Street refinement resolves inherited stratigraphy but does not lithify old deposits again simply to add map detail.
items.Other process interactions: Follows marine, lacustrine and river sediment deposition; compaction changes ground resistance and groundwater exchange. Reworked lithified material later enters erosion/transport; burial heat and pressure can feed metamorphism. Ordinary evaporites may provide a physical setting for Salt magic without generating its magical stock by fiat.
items.Invariants / obligations: Rock must arise from a supported sediment or chemical reservoir; keep bed depth, order, mineral identity, material ancestry and distinctions between loose, partly hardened and consolidated deposits. Do not turn all sediment into bedrock at one epoch boundary or conflate physical salt crust with Salt-system magic.
items.Review notes: Sediment-to-rock process with an associated basin-precipitation mechanism. If chemical evaporite genesis needs its own semantic identity, split it by physical cause, not by helper function; preserve the shared stratigraphic result.

items.Semantic name: Heat- and pressure-driven transformation of retained rock
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Transform buried rock materials through heat-driven metamorphism and retained geological conditions.
items.Observable effects: Buried, folded or intruded strata become distinct metamorphic bands, toughened basement and contact aureoles; later erosion reveals resistant ridges, altered mineral assemblages and evidence of ancient mountain roots or igneous heat.
items.Fields & products read: The actual layered rock composition and depth, burial and tectonic pressure/strain, geothermal/igneous heating history and duration, retained metamorphic grade, fluid interactions where justified, and previously established material identity and structural fabric.
items.Fields & products written: Transformed retained rock strata, mineral/alteration and resistance changes, metamorphic grade/history and updated structural/material properties for exhumation, faulting and erosion; no separate cosmetic rock classification disconnected from the column.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Consumes named thermal, burial and pressure conditions through the ground/material modes. Igneous and tectonic processes generate the forcing; the rock owner transforms the affected beds, while erosion, fractured-fluid flow and construction read their changed properties.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: Actual heat/pressure episodes during World geological history, potentially with local contact transformations from real events. Finer Region/City/Street maps resolve inherited metamorphic contacts and lithology without a second ancient heating interval.
items.Other process interactions: Mountain construction and crustal burial establish pressure and depth; plutons, volcanism, geothermal heat and long-lived faults alter temperature. Weathering, hillslope failure, quarrying and river incision later expose or selectively remove the resulting transformed rock.
items.Invariants / obligations: Transformation requires the appropriate host rock, thermal/pressure exposure and affected depth, and preserves location, parent material and stratigraphic provenance. No spontaneous metamorphic rocks from a warm surface, no duplicate alteration on repeated present reads, and no material mass invented for variety.
items.Review notes: Distinct rock-material transformation phenomenon, not a heat-map classifier. Geological conditions own the forcing; metamorphism owns the actual change in the retained column.

items.Semantic name: Geological epoch baseline and causal-history capture
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Record the terrain-height reference for geological history so later epochs can compare the changing land against it.
items.Observable effects: Later geology can recognize what relief was raised, cut, buried or preserved since an earlier epoch, and a map may explain a valley's incision or the persistence of an old scarp without a second geological event.
items.Fields & products read: Present terrain/bedrock elevation and selected physical state, beginning-of-epoch reference surfaces, epoch identity and elapsed-time context, prior captured geological history, provenance of material changes and stable feature identities.
items.Fields & products written: Retained first-epoch/epoch-reference height, history snapshots and causal links needed to compare physical change, with epoch labels and source provenance. No material, water, load or elevation is physically changed by recording it.
items.Shared questions / coupling: A history/state recorder under the physical owner; erosion, deposition, uplift, ice, ocean and landform interpretations can consume its references. It does not decide when/where tectonics occur and must avoid reissuing domain commands.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: On actual World epoch boundaries and when capturing a child for later refinement; finer maps inherit/realize the relevant historical reference rather than creating a separate geological timeline. Recording itself has no elapsed process effect.
items.Other process interactions: Feeds identification of old terraces, uplifted landscapes, age-dependent ecological/rock development and landmark persistence; couples with material ledger, checkpointing, named-feature history and publication.
items.Invariants / obligations: Snapshots must be temporally ordered and refer to the matching state and geographic footprint; they may not backfill an invented baseline from a cropped present. Idempotent recording must not double-advance history or modify the parent.
items.Review notes: State/history capture, not a geomorphic process. Preserve history information useful for causally credible refinement without demanding full raw-field archival for every epoch.

items.Semantic name: Population establishment and first settlement
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Establish living population and early settlement where human history actually begins, with physical resources, travel access and existing cultures affecting where origins succeed. Region/City refinement does not found the same people again.
items.Observable effects: A previously uninhabited world acquires inhabited areas and first settlement relationships; later fine-scale maps develop farmsteads, towns and urban concentrations from inherited population through other coupled spatial processes, not another population-creation event.
items.Fields & products read: Existing Population; `wildYield`, `livable`; water/habitable terrain.
items.Fields & products written: Population layer via human owner's `lay` operation.
items.Shared questions / coupling: `wildYield`, `livable`; population owner; ecological productivity and physical/magical habitability.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: Actual World genesis/colonization and distinct supported historical resettlement events. At Region/City/Street, initial population is supplied by generic sampling; use current spatial differentiation mechanisms instead of refounding inherited people.
items.Other process interactions: Precedes feeding, growth, migration and settlement construction; relies on ecology and terrain for founding sites.
items.Invariants / obligations: No new heads or independent cultural founding merely because a coarse cell is subdivided. Initial people and identities must have a plausible source; an unnamed local cluster need not become a historically new settlement.
items.Review notes: Retain as a genuinely historical population-origin process. New fine-grained nuclei within an inhabited parent are emergent *arrangements* made by movement, exchange and land development, not more people created by founding.

items.Semantic name: Demographic growth, mortality and survival pressure
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Advance population through births and deaths under actual elapsed human history, responding to viability, disease/harm, long-term provisioning and displacement. Offer living-condition and demographic-pressure context at finer scale without a new history pass.
items.Observable effects: World history can produce population growth, decline and survivor distributions, including delayed famine and damage. Region/City refinement reveals present differences in settlement viability and crowding but does not create babies or deaths to make a city-shaped raster.
items.Fields & products read: Existing Population and cultural/identity shares, historical reproductive/mortality exposure and elapsed time, food/market imports and storage, disease/harm, local housing pressure, physical and magical conditions, external support and migration context.
items.Fields & products written: During actual elapsed World history: updated numerical Population and associated identity shares, causal demographic events/history. During child spatial refinement: derived viability, housing/food stress or settlement pressure supplied to population movement and built-land processes, not new historical deaths/births.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Provisioning/markets influence sustained demographic prospects, not an instantaneous local carrying-capacity cap. Shared housing-capacity, harm, health and livability responses come from other domain owners; the population writer alone applies genuine demographic changes.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: World historical eras: true birth/death rates and elapsed exposure. Region/City/Street: current-state viability/pressure questions or no-op on demographics; iterations produce spatial organization without another century of population loss.
items.Other process interactions: Food trade, settlement concentration and housing capacity affect pressure; epidemics, weather, magic, siege and disasters influence genuine historic survival. The Region pattern is formed through gather, exchange and construction feedback, not this process's mortality loop.
items.Invariants / obligations: Do not set Population to locally grown food or housing stock. Import connections and stores matter; deaths demand historical exposure and mechanism. The parent city's rough headcount must survive child refinement except for justified comparable-footprint or genuine newly elapsed consequences.
items.Review notes: Keep the demographic process, but remove the regional pseudo-history role. In the pilot, a diagnostic must distinguish births/deaths from spatial moves: refinement iterations alone may not change total people through this contract.

items.Semantic name: Built-ground expansion, intensification and reuse
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Generate and evolve human construction on land, including diffuse farmsteads, compact settlements, intensive urban cores, crowded low-investment districts and abandonment, through construction and land-competition feedback—not a fixed Population-to-BuiltUp conversion.
items.Observable effects: Existing land use differentiates into dispersed rural construction, dense compact quarters, trading strips, wealthy low-occupancy estates, informal crowded neighborhoods and persistent ruined districts. Built land can intensify without spreading; population can increase without automatically increasing coverage; low wealth need not imply few residents.
items.Fields & products read: Population and occupancy pressure, inherited BuiltUp/Standing and ruins, rural land use, available natural ground, access and trade/craft/wealth, material and labor availability, institutional services, maintenance/physical-hazard effects, field location and comparable parent-scale built quantities.
items.Fields & products written: World genuine construction/abandonment: changes to BuiltUp area share, retained Standing investment/constructed stock and ruins via human-owner operations. Region: differentiated spatial coverage and relative construction intensity/usable capacity of inherited stock without another historical construction campaign. Built state is not created in fixed proportion to resident count.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Shared `building`, `wealth`, travel/access, constructed-service, crowding, support, hazard and maintenance questions; construction and investment can reinforce economic centers, while scarcity and decay limit use. Population moves in its own process, and many environmental/social processes change the same retained built stocks through typed owner modes.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: World historical building/investment, decay/abandonment over true elapsed time. Region nonhistorical nonlinear spatial realization with competing expansion, intensification, reuse, scarce land and regional layout feedback. City/Street progressively resolve later geometry; individual structures are not required for Region.
items.Other process interactions: Feeds built capacity, spatial attraction and crowding back to gather and trade; competes with farmland/pasture and ecology; water, animals, climate, magic and siege affect damage/care through maintenance and event responses. Later town/construction details draw from the numeric state, not vice versa at Region.
items.Invariants / obligations: Never use `BuiltUp = Population / fixed_density` or `Standing = BuiltUp * fixed_wealth` as the definition of the phenomenon. Keep extent, investment/intensity and condition distinguishable and causally co-produced; don't automatically invent past construction from extra cells or demand one footprint/parcel per person.
items.Review notes: Major redesign of this existing semantic process; no new generic urban-density/noise process. `BuiltUp` measures developed area, `Standing` existing works/capital and ruins retain abandoned material; test their joint ability to express capacity and condition before adding numeric stocks. Any new field must be changed/read by multiple meaningful processes and preserve single-writer operations.

items.Semantic name: Food production, provisioning and land-use allocation
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Develop cultivation, grazing, foraging and food provisioning through real history; at finer scales differentiate productive land and market-supply relationships from inherited stocks and current terrain, without refiring historical hunger.
items.Observable effects: Fertile valleys, pasture rims, worked rural country and market-provisioned urban centers organize into contrasting land-use patterns. A dense city can occupy little farmland and remain provisioned through accessible villages, trade and hinterland suppliers beyond the visible map.
items.Fields & products read: Inherited Farmland, Pasture, agricultural suitability and ecological yields, soil/water/land cover, cultivation labor, seasonal food stores, existing food supply and transport trade, demand from *resident* people, outside-market production and real historical time when applicable.
items.Fields & products written: World time: agricultural land-use and food stocks or supply relationships, harvest/surplus and historically justified hunger pressures. Region spatial solve: differentiated farmland/pasture distribution, reachable food access and provisioning context; no new population deaths or unsupported crop history.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Typed yield, transport, food imports, market exchange and household needs supply actual provisioning; finite production/supply and reachable connections constrain viability. `human.land.gather` and construction can favor sites supported by markets without equating urban density to local crop yield.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: World historical agricultural/market evolution with elapsed seasons/eras. Region/City: present-state spatial allocation and coupled refinement of inherited productive lands and off-map supply, with several nonlinear passes but no extra growing seasons or starvation.
items.Other process interactions: Trade carries countryside food to cities; rural cultivation competes with built coverage and natural habitat; farmstead accessibility and population/crafts affect where land is worked. Soil, weather and animals condition the result via common questions.
items.Invariants / obligations: Retain credible total rural land occupation and supply over comparable areas; do not impose exactly equal farmland on every child or force a city to feed itself from its own 800 km² World cell. Boundary providers must represent suppliers outside the cropped map.
items.Review notes: Retain as a causal food/land-use phenomenon. In Region refinement its output is patterned agriculture and provisioned *access*, not a population-capacity mask causing historical deaths. Food can organize rural farms and cities without a direct food→headcount conversion.

items.Semantic name: Goods exchange, market formation and transport centrality
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Evolve goods exchange, markets and reachable commercial ties in historical time; at finer resolution generate market cores, corridors, competing trading centers and periphery from existing economic relationships and local access.
items.Observable effects: Ports, crossroads, established routes and competing exchanges develop economic concentrations; prosperous cores can support intensive building, while peripheral farmsteads, low-service neighborhoods or trade-deficient towns develop differently. Several market nodes can emerge from one coarse cell.
items.Fields & products read: Inherited trade/wealth and goods relationships, real producers and customers, population, cultivated land and constructed capacity, routes and travel friction, river/sea/Veil links, place offerings, hazards, external supplier/client flows and current map geometry.
items.Fields & products written: World history: movement of actual goods, trade and wealth effects and worn way records when journeys truly occur. Regional spatial solve: differentiated market-access, commercial pressure, invested-capital opportunity and viable local corridor structure; no fictitious goods turnover or historical road wear.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Economic centrality emerges from network exchange and demand↔access↔built capacity feedback, not a hard-coded city point or an independent 'market intensity' decoration. Shared goods, travel, wealth and draw questions feed population movement and built-land development.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: World: elapsed goods production/exchange, network use and investments. Region: iterative present spatial realization of inherited economic influence and access, including external markets, with no repeated years of trade or travel wear. City: finer junction and district variants of the same exchange phenomenon.
items.Other process interactions: Food suppliers, population centers, craft producers and institutions create markets; roads and waterways provide access; trade influences where capital accumulates, maintenance is affordable and buildings intensify or decline.
items.Invariants / obligations: No invented cargo from a settlement label, no fabricated roads or wealth without activity. Multiple competing or overlapping centers may emerge. A cropped hinterland cannot be treated as no external trade or the sole source of a parent city's goods.
items.Review notes: Retain and strengthen; the regional variant is a *generative spatial exchange/centrality mechanism*, not a read-only suitability map. No mandatory separate trade-center process or points extracted from World-scale records.

items.Semantic name: Population attraction, migration and multiscale spatial organization
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Redistribute people according to access, markets, livelihood, support, crowding and risk; advance real migration in World history and generate finer present-day settlement concentrations through nonhistorical interacting spatial passes on child maps.
items.Observable effects: From initially similar inherited fine cells, network interaction differentiates dense urban centers, competing towns, fringes, villages, dispersed farmsteads and low-population country. Trade, access and construction reinforce concentration while crowding, rural livelihood and hazards oppose it; no preselected World point is necessary.
items.Fields & products read: Inherited Population and identity distributions as provisional samples, existing BuiltUp/Standing/ruins and capacity pressures, markets/goods and food access, travel and cross-boundary roads, terrain, hazards, local room and regional settlements as *rough contextual facts*, not exact anchors.
items.Fields & products written: World: actual demographic migration, relocations and traveled-route use. Region/City: reorganized Population and accompanying identity shares over finer cells, responsive spatial concentration and reduced/increased crowding; no birth/death, made-up history, route wear or new person stock.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Spatial feedback with trade, feeding and construction: market access draws people; occupation raises demand and investments; built capacity attracts or limits density; hazards and land scarcity create competing gradients. Use society-owner movement/apportion modes with causal interactions, not one combined weighted mask.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: World historical movement: elapsed exposure and genuine migration through the global network. Region: repeated nonlinear *present spatial organization* across child cells and external context, not per-parent-cell isolated ranking. City: same semantic movement, with neighborhood/road/edge strategies folded in from former `human.city.growth`. Street: use if population detail is represented at that fidelity.
items.Other process interactions: Trade and place benefits make centers, agricultural livelihoods support dispersed rural population, built investment creates capacity, congestion and hazard repel, road/water/Veil connectivity changes reach. Other processes' outputs change attractors during the same refinement solve.
items.Invariants / obligations: Preserve approximately credible population for comparable geographic regions and inherited identity shares; parent-cell borders are not travel barriers. Do not invent an urban point from extracted World GIS, force a single circular city, rerun years, or rely on an independent City growth process to repair a diffuse Region.
items.Review notes: Canonical semantic population-organization process. Fold `human.city.growth` into this process as the City-fidelity strategy. The process itself, not generic inheritance or feature extraction, creates urban spatial complexity.

items.Semantic name: Adoption of magical crafts
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Spread the practice of magical crafts among inhabitants where their corresponding magical media offer opportunities to learn.
items.Observable effects: Where a magical medium is present and people can learn to practice it, a share of residents becomes keepers of that craft. The distribution of practitioners can later influence magical rule breaks, trade goods, local access and the character of realms.
items.Fields & products read: Population and existing identity/craft holdings; each registered magical craft's medium/availability; elapsed years.
items.Fields & products written: Craft tradition within society's identity columns, through the human owner's `overlay` operation; not a change to total population.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Craft medium, trade, cultural contact, access and actual practitioner holdings jointly create local differentiation; magnetic field or arbitrary intensity alone does not imply a practitioner. The same people/craft identity stocks and owner operations remain authoritative.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: World: actual elapsed craft learning/adoption where people and magical media interact. Region/City: realize current practitioner concentration around inherited medium, routes, practice and trade opportunities without another cycle of historical teaching.
items.Other process interactions: Depends on magic media and current practitioner distribution; learned crafts change magic-rule responses, specialty goods/trade, craft suitability in migration and realm characterization.
items.Invariants / obligations: Craft adoption changes practice, not headcount. Preserve inherited craft populations and commitments during refinement; do not rerun centuries of learning merely because a child has finer cells.
items.Review notes: Keep the independent cultural/practice phenomenon. Its Region strategy may spatially differentiate already inherited practitioner counts, feeding craft-market and housing attraction without adding new historical conversions.

items.Semantic name: Capture environmental exposure baseline
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Retain environmental reference conditions needed to apply subsequent burial, scouring, flooding and impacts to people and built land.
items.Observable effects: Records the terrain-change baseline so later social response can distinguish new inundation, deposition, scour and impacts from already established history.
items.Fields & products read: Cumulative deposition, glacial deposition/erosion, volcanic construction and impact history; prior `human_land_seen`.
items.Fields & products written: `human_land_seen` retained comparison bands for laid, stripped and struck ground.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Physical cumulative-history bands; society environmental-response/capture contract.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: World historical physical checkpointing and initial-condition capture; child refinement imports relevant completed exposure history rather than capturing a fake intervening era.
items.Other process interactions: Provides the baseline for `human.land.meet`; should track the geology/ice/water processes that alter human land.
items.Invariants / obligations: An inherited history must not be interpreted as a fresh environmental impact; checkpointing should be consistent across a refinement boundary.
items.Review notes: Non-process physical-to-society history checkpoint; paired with `human.land.meet`'s causal response. Never make a new exposure event just because generic sampling and regional spatial iterations completed.

items.Semantic name: Human settlement response to physical and ecological forcing
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Apply actual new environmental damage, protection and burial/exposure to people and constructed land during historical events, and supply differentiated current hazard/condition exposure for spatial refinement without replaying prior disasters.
items.Observable effects: Coastal floods, severe storms, fires, wildlife encroachment, ice, erosion and magical hazards distinguish viable dense cores from vulnerable fringes and derelict areas; sheltered or maintained districts can remain functional. Inherited ruined ground remains part of the land's history rather than disappearing as the child is generated.
items.Fields & products read: Current physical change versus retained environmental checkpoints; existing Population, BuiltUp, Standing and ruin state; flood/heat/erosion/ice/animal intrusion, supported protection or magic effects; inherited damage history and out-of-footprint source context.
items.Fields & products written: World genuinely new hazards: human-owner wear, burial and re-exposure, surviving people and materially justified built-capacity/condition loss. Region: current differentiated hazard and protection forcing for gather, harden and maintenance; no second time-dependent loss merely from evaluating exposure.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Responds through shared `harm`, `livable`, building-durability/exposure, water and material effect modes. Ecology, animals, magic, hydrology, climate and tectonics supply causes; the human owner applies all damage to the retained built/population state rather than multiple copied housing simulations.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: World: after new physical changes with real elapsed impact and a recorded baseline. Region/City: conditioning on present local exposures and inherited damage, not an additional flood/eruption/storm. Genuine newly caused local material change can still use appropriate cause-specific application.
items.Other process interactions: Forces repairs and abandonment through promoted built maintenance, affects people movement and built intensification; ecological succession can recolonize abandoned lots; siege and disasters are separate historic causes with shared damage modes.
items.Invariants / obligations: No repeated damage if the current exposure is simply a finer interpretation of the parent past. Distinguish historic hazard events from present susceptibility; track cause, material/stock changes and boundaries, not just hazard colors.
items.Review notes: Keep as environmental/built coupling, not a second climate, animal or disaster engine. Separate exposure evaluation from history-changing wear and coordinate with built maintenance to avoid double deterioration.

items.Semantic name: Society refinement initialization and process coordination
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Coordinate the society domain's child initial state and schedule its scale-specific semantic-process strategies after generic lattice sampling; do not independently decide the detailed population or built-land pattern with one aggregate suitability-weighting function.
items.Observable effects: The child begins with legitimate coarse people, agricultural, built and identity stocks; subsequent trade, movement, food, construction and maintenance interactions generate differentiated farmsteads, villages, cities and countryside. The coordinator creates no extra settlement phenomenon.
items.Fields & products read: Already sampled parent Population, Farmland, Pasture, BuiltUp, Standing, ruins and identities; parent-to-child location relations and broad historical/identity constraints; available region/adjacent external context, execution stage and capability declarations.
items.Fields & products written: Bound initial-condition products, compatibility of source/receiver stocks, and scheduling/diagnostic products; the **semantic processes** own the differentiated Population, agricultural land, BuiltUp/Standing and identity updates. Generic copying belongs to lattice/resource inheritance.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Composes typed process contracts and providers, supplies parent-derived budgets/contexts and connects boundary sources; replaces the existing one-shot shared weight for Population/BuiltUp/Standing with separate interacting causal strategies.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: Region, City, Street refinement startup/iteration coordination only. No elapsed demographic, construction, trade, culture or physical history; outer map creation remains an agnostic sampler.
items.Other process interactions: Orchestrates land.gather, land.trade, land.feed and land.harden plus maintenance and relevant effects. `human.places.record` interprets the resulting density and attaches known identity afterward rather than seeding an invented World point.
items.Invariants / obligations: Does not independently apportion all human layers by one fixed 'room' field, impose hard per-parent-cell borders or invent an authoritative city center. Initial numeric totals/identities are constraints over comparable geographic areas, not the final spatial arrangement.
items.Review notes: RECLASSIFY as non-semantic coordination. This legacy ID should not remain a listed causal process once the scale-conditioned society variants are registered; keep its row only for migration/provenance. Generic numerical inheritance remains untouched.

items.Semantic name: Settlement identity, history and emergent geographic recognition
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Recognize population/built-land concentrations and historic ruins after the semantic processes have generated them; reconcile those patterns with inherited named settlement identity and rough census without dictating a precise World-scale point location.
items.Observable effects: Observed centers, multiple urban cores, dispersed villages, farmstead country and ruin complexes become identifiable places after settlement spatial dynamics. A named city is matched to appropriate resulting development rather than forced to exist at an arbitrary world-extracted coordinate.
items.Fields & products read: Generated Population, BuiltUp, Standing, developed intensity, ways/markets, comparable inherited broad settlement identity/rough population and vicinity, historical founding/ruin context; observed spatial connectivity and footprints rather than authoritative World-point coordinates.
items.Fields & products written: Reconciled place identities, approximate current census within meaningful recognized extents, geographic footprints/catchments and history references; named stable places and later GIS candidates. No new people, built stock, source effects or historical route wear from classification.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Reads the emergent society field and its economic/land-use network; existing place ID, rough history and count are recognition constraints. If several candidate centers exist, interpret their relationship to the known city using geography and context; do not dictate a radial template.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: World historical place recognition and identity capture when history actually advances; Region/City present-state recognition after nonlinear spatial refinement. No fictional new city founder, abandonment event or elapsed migration merely because a center is detected at another resolution.
items.Other process interactions: Serves places, political identity, historic migration and GIS publication; city extraction is *downstream* of gather/trade/harden/food rather than the causal engine for those processes at Region.
items.Invariants / obligations: A World point placed by feature extraction is not authoritative subcell truth. Preserve an existing name/identity and roughly credible census without imposing a pin or fixed footprint. No named city vanishes when the finer pattern becomes multi-centered or moves within broad conditions.
items.Review notes: Change role emphasis: identity matching and geographic interpretation, not fine settlement construction. Existing World-scale points must not be used as mandatory attractors in the Region pilot; assess place matching only after population and built state have emerged.

items.Semantic name: Origins of tongues, faiths and customs
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Establish initial tongues, faiths, and customs among populations and record their cultural origins.
items.Observable effects: Distinct cultural origin groups arise at selected inhabited sites, with their own tongues, faiths and customs. Connected inhabited territory receives an originating cultural identity from reachable founding centers.
items.Fields & products read: Existing population and identity columns; existing tradition records; configured cultural founder count; travel friction, climbing, rivers and traversable links; map geometry.
items.Fields & products written: Founding tradition/entity records (tongue, faith, custom) and founding origin positions; Tongue, Faith and Custom identities assigned via the human owner's `overlay` operation.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Culture/identity records and origin memory; travel and spatial nearest-origin lookup; `travelFriction`, `climbing`, river/link routes; owner overlays.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: Culture founding on an initially unassigned inhabited world during a human era; origins influence reachable populations beyond immediately adjacent cells.
items.Other process interactions: Gives cultural identities to subsequent contact, language learning, divergence, realm formation, settlement characterization and publication.
items.Invariants / obligations: Do not re-found or overwrite established inherited cultures on a child map. Origin records and identities must persist as the same culture across refinement; founding assigns identities to people without manufacturing extra population.

items.Semantic name: Cultural contact, adoption and language learning
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Spread and change cultural practices through contact and travel, including language learning, adoption, and fading use.
items.Observable effects: People encounter other tongues, faiths and customs through travel; some adopt unfamiliar practices, while language contact produces both native-speaker transitions and second-language knowledge. Rarely used second languages may fade.
items.Fields & products read: Existing identity columns and leading Tongue, Faith, Custom and Known language; population; human-era years/mobility; reachable travel network and contacts; `forgetting` answer and neighbors' language use.
items.Fields & products written: Identity column overlays for Tongue, Faith, Custom and Known language; changes in local adoption and second-language retention via the human owner.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Travel-cost reach over roads, rivers and links; `forgetting` shared question; contact pressure from neighboring populations; identity owner `overlay`; language use from the surrounding community.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: World human eras: true cultural exchange, language learning and adoption through time. Region/City: local realization of current language distributions using connections, mixed settlement access and retained historical contact, not new generations of language evolution.
items.Other process interactions: Follows founding; propagates cultures across social/trade networks; shared language can lower travel costs, enabling more contact and migration; influences cultural borders, traditions and later realm allegiance.
items.Invariants / obligations: Cultural transitions retain population/identity mass; knowledge of an additional tongue is not equivalent to changing primary speech. Refinement must inherit contact results instead of simulating an extra historical era.
items.Review notes: Keep language contact as meaningful cross-scale culture; regional spatial patterning uses the same interaction/transport causes as history, but no new historical fluency years.

items.Semantic name: Geographic divergence of cultures
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Form daughter tongues or customs where sizable groups become geographically separated from their parent tradition.
items.Observable effects: When substantial, disconnected groups become isolated from the main body of a tongue or custom, daughter traditions can emerge with a recorded connection to the parent.
items.Fields & products read: Leading Tongue and Custom identities, population distribution, active tradition registry, era, geographic connectivity, travel costs and traversable links.
items.Fields & products written: New daughter tongue/custom origin records with parent links; relabeling of the geographically separated identity columns through the human owner's `rename` operation.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Travel and `country::spread` connectivity; the society tradition-memory catalogue; `leading_of` identity reads; owner `rename`.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: Historical cultural divergence over regions separated beyond the configured travel reach; evaluates disconnected groups relative to the parent tradition's total population.
items.Other process interactions: Acts after founding and contact; creates differences that influence later contact, shared-language travel, cultural publication and potentially political cohesion. Does not directly sunder faiths in the current implementation.
