items.Invariants / obligations: Preserve genealogy and identity of already-established daughter traditions. Do not invent new schisms because a child map is cropped or has smaller cells; a divergence must represent genuine geographic/social separation, not a missing boundary input.

items.Semantic name: Political realm founding
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Found political realms around suitable inhabited seats and retain their originating relationship to existing allegiances.
items.Observable effects: Inhabited settlement seats establish identifiable political realms. First realms arise at distinct populated centers; additional seats beyond existing realms' effective reach can found independent or daughter realms, creating distinct histories and future centers of authority.
items.Fields & products read: Living, nonabsorbed named towns and their population/anchors; existing realm seats and tradition memory; local leading Allegiance and Tongue; political realm-count/reach settings; travel costs and links.
items.Fields & products written: New realm/allegiance identity and entity records, including origin, founding era, founding tongue, optional parent allegiance and a persistent seat-place ID. Founding alone does not allocate allegiance to population.

items.Semantic name: Political reach, allegiance and rivalry

Seat population, food-supported health, institutions, craft suitability, ruins and incumbent loyalty shape reach; strong rivals contest towns, seats can move or fail, and places outside all reach can lose allegiance.

Preserve established realm IDs and allegiance distribution across refinement without replaying political change.

items.Semantic name: Engineered water-control boundary and context adapter

Treat these as facets of the same **waterworks↔hydrology context contract**, not two separate semantic processes. Inherited/geographic boundary handling needs an explicit provider.

items.Semantic name: City-fidelity strategy of population attraction and movement

Consider folding the wrapper into caller binding rather than preserving an unnecessary public orchestration ID. Do not split the settlement phenomenon merely because the current code has Atlas and Field layers.

items.Semantic name: Cultural-era orchestration
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Coordinate culture formation, contact, divergence, and retention over a human historical era.

items.Semantic name: Political-era orchestration
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Coordinate the formation and development of realms, including political competition and allegiance during a human era.

items.Semantic name: Societal hazards, siege, famine, flight and event aftermath
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Generate and apply social disruption—sieges, hazards, threats, disasters, and the movement of survivors—while recording their consequences.
items.Observable effects: Over actual history, famine is recorded, location-specific hazards and magical confluences strike towns, contested takeovers lead to sieges, living populations and standing works suffer loss, and survivors move to reachable refuge; persistent event records explain the resulting ruins and demographic shifts.
items.Fields & products read: Living/ruined Places and their era histories; realm/allegiance state and contest markers; `harm`, `support`, `livable`, `travelFriction`, `climbing`, rivers, traversable links; hazard exposures, catalogue magic-meeting rates/coverage; years, event RNG and available destination room.
items.Fields & products written: Human-owner `wear` and survivor `move_layer` effects on Population and built/standing layers; route use as applicable; event records with kind, cause, location, casualties, displacement/refuge, severity and era; place-specific event hooks and ruin consequences.
items.Shared questions / coupling: `harm` and habitable/support room questions, regional physical hazards and each named magic meeting; realm takeover contest, travel and flight; society owner wear/move and place catalogue event hook.

Different magical hazards retain their own causes and physical character. Movement requires reachable capacity; histories retain identity and era linkage.
items.Review notes: Still a meaningful social-disruption family. Current implementation bundles sieges, other hazards and flight; revisit constituent process ownership later, without deleting the phenomena. | Current `land_events.rs` wraps famine, ordinary hazard draws, magic-meeting threats, sieges and refugee flight in one `human.events` command. Its generic burn/shake mix for all magic meetings loses the lore's differentiated mechanisms; consider independently owned disaster/siege/flight processes with a coordinating event lifecycle, without removing phenomena. | DECISION — split siege warfare into its own semantic process; `human.events` should coordinate/record siege events and aftermath, not own siege mechanics. The siege contract must cover blockade/provisioning, defenses and assault, casualties, damage to built ground/standing works, refugees and political outcomes, without replaying historical sieges during refinement.

items.Semantic name: Society-built dam construction, retention and failure
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Establish, retain, or abandon dams and other society-built water controls, including their effects on standing water and drainage.
items.Observable effects: In historical society development, settlements attempt dams at river sites, confirm that they impound a meaningful lake, retain accepted works, and allow works to fail after abandonment. Their presence changes the hydrological network and leaves attributable landscape and settlement consequences.
items.Fields & products read: Living named Places, their abandonment/absorption; retained Works/previously attempted sites; river order, flow and channel/water state; existing authored dams; actual historical era and the physical river system.
items.Fields & products written: Persistent Works records for accepted dams, failures and rejected/dry trials; current engineered dam constraints through its adapter; routed river/lake state recomputed by physical hydrology owner; later GIS publication via `human.water-present`.

items.Spatial & temporal scope: Actual society-history events when an inhabited place can build and maintain a dam; existing structures and authored works become present boundary/input conditions for Region/City/Street. Child refinement does not found/abandon historic dams again.
items.Other process interactions: Requires living place and suitable river, tests impoundment before retention; alters hydrology and access, potentially feeds or displaces nearby society; final waters extracted by `human.water-present` and dam features by the POI catalogue.
items.Invariants / obligations: A dam is a discrete identified work at a supported site, not a fractional mark in every cell. Accept it only if physical impoundment works; retain authored/protected and already established works. Apply historical construction/failure once; carry upstream/downstream impacts across cropped map edges.
items.Review notes: Current `dam_sites::trials` selects river-adjacent sites, `judge` accepts only when new lake cells appear; `fail_abandoned` retires works when their supporting place dies. Separate waterworks evolution from dam constraint binding and GIS refresh, but retain one substantive dam process.

items.Semantic name: Current magic-state binding for society-era interactions

Its effects depend on the separate current-magic producer, so classify as binding/context, not a new process. Actual source renewal remains owned by magic processes.

items.Semantic name: Present water-state reconciliation and GIS publication after human works
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Apply and realize the hydrological consequences of human-built waterworks in the current water state and published geography.

items.Fields & products read: Waterworks change flag and standing/drawn dam sites; current river/lake physical fields and channels; prior GIS water features/networks, protected/landmark/related/crossed features; publication selection and map geometry.

Preserve protected, landmark, referenced and crossed features; stable water identity and network continuity; no double evolution, no deletion of authored water, no reconciling away historical geography.

The current delete-and-reextract logic deserves special identity review under ADR 0009, especially for named rivers/lakes. Not a separately timed hydrology process.

That gating may need review for first-time regional/current publication, but it is not a new semantic magic process.

items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Publish the present spatial population-density and food-support fields as map products.

items.Semantic name: Political geography and administration publication
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Realize political geography—sovereignty, control, claims and administration—from the established realms and allegiances.

items.Semantic name: Settlement, works and travel-network GIS realization
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Realize settlements, built structures and travel networks as geographic features from the society's retained state and place catalogue.
items.Observable effects: Materializes generated inhabited places, ruins, major settlement structures and significant roads/ways as readable GIS features, including late society-moment catalogue POIs, causal provenance and meaningful connections.
items.Fields & products read: Current retained population/building/works state, Places/ways and society-era history; catalogue source/POI entries, physical habitat, water and geographic support; configured highway and significance selection, current known feature identities.
items.Fields & products written: Published settlement, works and route GIS records with geometry, identity, relations and descriptive causes; late society POI publication and domain-level provenance entry. Does not run feeding, building, migration or settlement founding.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Atlas `publish_places` / catalogue `places.late` / `publish_ways`; links numerical Society+POI record ownership to GIS feature extraction, history and stable geographic identities.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: Published map output at an appropriate post-society stage: World present-day geography and equivalent spatial realization at finer map types/fidelities. No elapsed history or fresh local building process hidden in publication.
items.Other process interactions: Consumes outcomes of `human.places.record`, human waterworks, infrastructure/travel, cultural/political histories and town/city development. Feeds the map viewer, POI registry, district refinement and authored GIS workflows.
items.Invariants / obligations: A published place/road is supported by actual society and canonical source identity; do not invent residents or infrastructure by printing a feature. Preserve named POIs across refinement, significant landmarks, authored/protected GIS products and network endpoint consistency. No regeneration of completed history.
items.Review notes: Output realization of existing society settlements, works and roads; does not substitute for the underlying construction/travel mechanisms. | Current `atlas/people/built.rs` calls `state.publish_places`, late society-moment catalogue publication and `publish_ways`; `built.layout` is a misleading generative label for a GIS publisher. Treat actual town layout/construction as separate processes in Chunk 5.

items.Semantic name: Settlement founding and inhabited kernel
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Found an inhabited settlement from existing people, traversable ground, resources, connections and institutions. Establish an initial spatial kernel and its governing development constraints; founding is a causal social/geographic act, not an initialization utility.
items.Observable effects: A viable settlement begins at a meaningful site: an occupied landing, defended shelf, crossroads, orchard, sanctuary, guild common or other supported kernel. Its initial access, shared space, tenure and premises constrain subsequent growth and leave a legible founding form.
items.Fields & products read: Inherited named settlement and approximate resident population; local terrain/water/habitability, actual access and external routes, productive opportunities, cultural or political institutions, magical media/maintained links; feasible founding templates, existing selected template/site evidence, existing works and established rights.
items.Fields & products written: Retained settlement kernel, first occupied parcels/premises, accessible paths and relationships, initial tenure/founding identity, and persistent chosen template rules. City handoff also exposes the selected template's eligible district type/program vocabulary and each role's causal prerequisites and emphatic physical morphology (open spaces, developed intensity, routes, rights, precinct/defense connections), along with compatible district/Street guidance. Does not create inhabitants, magical sources, a second historical founding or an unrelated polity.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Site-selection questions and place-catalogue offers supply causal opportunities; physical and magic owners provide present media and risks; settlement and society owners agree on the inherited place identity. Founding templates express eligible spatial arrangements, not predestined political types.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: Found a previously unrealized town from supported site evidence; when a City map refines a known settlement, carry its established kernel, template choice, institutions and origin forward rather than refounding or replaying history. City and district/Street strategies consume the same selected template at their respective fidelities.
items.Other process interactions: At City generation, provide the selected eligible founding template's persistent City policies PLUS its district-type palette, spatial signatures, eligible functional roles, rights, density/open-space preferences, alignments, fortified/gate needs and district/Street refinement relationships. Town.districts SELECTS and spatially negotiates supported strong district types; movement, land competition, investment and construction consume their active programs. The template itself remains a constraint/producer of options, not a finished city stamp; major works independently qualify by their own site and sponsor evidence.
items.Invariants / obligations: Founding requires actual habitation and operational access; a named existing town cannot disappear because a local kernel candidate is unsuitable. Do not assign ideology, slavery, zealotry, craft or wealth from a visual template alone; inheritance/realization must supply the missing supporting context.
items.Review notes: Owner correction: the selected City template must actively inform which district types are viable and how strongly they are expressed at City scale, not merely provide passive street alignment. Carry type/program guidance into finer District/Street maps.

items.Semantic name: City circulation and local street development
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Create and adapt functional access networks that connect existing settlement activity, external approach routes, district destinations and future buildable frontages. City strategy produces a continuous hierarchy of major thoroughfares and crossings; Street strategy resolves local streets, paths and entries within inherited city geometry.
items.Observable effects: Major routes join districts, docks, public squares, markets, residences, work sites and outside corridors into a recognizable city-wide skeleton. Dense quarters have local street permeability and civic precincts their own approach geometry; terrain, water, land rights and trade cause irregularity rather than decorative disconnected spikes.
items.Fields & products read: Inherited external/Regional routes, river/harbor crossings and continuing trade links; strong City stencil to favor major urban connectivity INSIDE without cutting outside roads; EARLY town.districts type programs and their characteristic access/approach/axis needs; selected City template policy, inhabited/working destinations, civic/defensive commitments, land claims, numeric population/built stock, terrain/water/hazards, named routes, gate proposals and available means.
items.Fields & products written: Persistent connected City main-route network, external approach continuations to satellite markets/farms/waystations, crossings, access classes, gate-aligned connections and major precinct approaches; Street-scale subordinate routes and entries. Real route construction/land occupation is shared with proper owners and never duplicates inherited travel-time history.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Accessibility and travel demand from society, economic activity and institutions drive routes. District partition and construction consume the network, while their new spatial decisions feed back to refine viable connections and access gaps.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: City: coherent primary circulation and connections over the whole City context (main urban body, fringe, and supported outlying places), with major routes, barriers and gateway constraints. Street: smaller local streets and access to premises within fixed City districts/major routes. World/Region long-distance connectivity belongs to existing broader movement and trade processes.
items.Other process interactions: Template alignment and EARLY typed district programs shape the City primary network before fixation (administrative/ceremonial approaches, commercial freight, guarded entries, broad estate routes, congested/poorly invested quarters where supported). Stencil interior strongly biases urban destinations and connectivity, while external routes, gates, markets, satellite hamlets and road stops continue outside. Co-iterate with land competition, investment, construction and district programs; inherit final district boundaries but do not use them to forbid through-routes.
items.Invariants / obligations: Every significant developed area—including supported suburban and outlying sites—should have plausible reachable access, with deliberate exceptions for isolated sites. Maintain external route continuity, named crossings and usable gates; do not mistake the City urban core boundary or City map edge for an impassable barrier. No ornamental disconnected stubs, no City boundary rewrite at Street fidelity, and no repeated historical road wear.
items.Review notes: City major thoroughfares must visibly respond to the selected template and distinctive early district programs, not only to a final density map. The stencil biases interior network prominence but does not terminate access at its edge.

items.Semantic name: Urban externalities and shared activity context
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Provide the locally available spatial context of economic exchange, waste load and other pressures that town mechanisms experience. This contract unifies the observations without claiming that one generic 'signal' is the cause of every pressure.
items.Observable effects: Active market corridors and densely used premises exert influence beyond their own footprints; waste and nuisance burden nearby places and waterways, enabling neighborhood differences in sanitation, rent, health and investment demand.
items.Fields & products read: Observed occupation, goods/visitor movements, workplaces, existing waste and services, route networks, local hydrology/slope, activity crossing the visible footprint and previously retained context where applicable.
items.Fields & products written: Typed, spatially located exchange/access and waste/health-pressure products for consumers; persistent quantities only when the owning exchange or waste process legitimately evolves them. No direct creation of new houses, commerce or social population.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Coupling contract between settlement activity, sanitation, economic opportunity and environmental burden. Distinct processes own trade generation and waste production/transport; context exposes their compatible effects to town consumers through shared questions/providers.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: Current-map contextual read/assembly at City and Street scale, with explicit upstream context for long routes, visitors and waste entering the modeled footprint. May sample retained state, but should not infer new years of accumulation from repeated reads.
items.Other process interactions: Used by sanitation, maintenance, livelihood, construction and public investment; physically sourced changes in exchange or waste propagate through their respective owners rather than being attributed to this adapter.
items.Invariants / obligations: Repeat evaluation must not create additional waste, commerce or time-dependent change. Resolve external traffic and pollution context rather than assuming an isolated town. Exchange and waste should remain separately interpretable and not be hidden inside an untraceable scalar.
items.Review notes: Non-process coupling/context contract. The two actual phenomena—economic circulation and waste accumulation/transport—must remain causally distinguishable; whether each deserves a separate semantic catalog entry is a catalog-design question, not a verdict from a function name.

items.Semantic name: Premises viability, occupation and economic activity
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Resolve who can use housing, shops, workshops, services and productive holdings, and whether those uses remain viable under reachable opportunities, rights, supply, demand and local hazards.
items.Observable effects: Occupied houses and workplaces cluster near viable opportunities, while isolated shops close, institutions shift clientele, services emerge or shrink, and dense demand creates crowding and uneven prosperity. Dependence on trade, access and care leaves visible consequences.
items.Fields & products read: Established settlement population and identity, housing and workplace stock, household and institution rights, employment/production means, reachable partners and imports, transport routes, service needs, local environmental/magical affordances and hazards.
items.Fields & products written: Retained occupation and operating relationships, supported household/workplace capacity, demand and unmet need, site viability, investment resources and crowding pressure. Does not directly manufacture new society population or physical goods from a demand estimate.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Market/service offers are typed by producers and place contracts; transport provides costs, while society's food/trade network provides external economic context. Cultural affiliations and local magical craft matter only through supported practices, rules and material media.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: City/Street occupancy and local premise economic detail, conditional on the already-developed Region settlement and market patterns; no separate regional housing simulator or historical economic era.
items.Other process interactions: Drives construction demand, land intensification, traffic, institutional investment and maintenance capacity; changes to roads, crops, magic practice, floods or security feed back into the local economy.
items.Invariants / obligations: Do not create residents to fill buildings or erase an established city because its whole supply chain lies outside the map. Economic exchange, actual capacity and spatial reach must substantiate viability; conditions can improve or decline with time without arbitrary occupational archetypes.
items.Review notes: Keep for later premises detail. World/Region uses goods/market interactions in `human.land.trade` and movement/constructed-stock feedback, without first requiring individual work and housing premises.

items.Semantic name: Waste removal and urban environmental maintenance
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Remove, treat or relocate waste where settlement labor, routes, service infrastructure and physical sinks make sanitation possible.
items.Observable effects: Serviced corridors stay healthier and more attractive; unserved or low-lying neighborhoods accumulate refuse and contamination. Sewer, drainage or disposal access can alter property use and justify civic investment.
items.Fields & products read: Retained waste loads and inflows, water/terrain/drainage, occupied premises, service coverage and transport access, public/institutional capacity, current pollution from surrounding land and ongoing deposition mechanisms.
items.Fields & products written: Reduced or transferred waste burden, service effects, remaining pollution and localized environmental pressure. Transfers or disposal need actual receiving capacity; do not silently delete matter when the intended process transports it.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Settlement services couple to environmental waste/health state through a single owner; sanitation capacity derives from built infrastructure, labor, institutions or explicitly supplied public service, not an automatic cleanup factor.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: Local active sanitation or current-state service response at City and Street fidelity; historical aging/accumulation belongs to the appropriate elapsed waste process, not to each refresh or refinement.
items.Other process interactions: Influences livelihood, habitability, ecological water quality, building maintenance and institutional needs; drainage and floods can move contamination; construction/investment may add the infrastructure that enables clearance.
items.Invariants / obligations: No blanket 'clean town' postprocessing. Respect finite service capacity, barriers, discharge location, ownership and out-of-footprint waste. Repeated publication or unchanged-state refinement must not repeatedly subtract the same waste load.
items.Review notes: Semantic process: actual environmental service with spatially visible outcomes, distinct from a state-finalizer or map-cleaning step.

items.Semantic name: Urban intensification and parcel competition
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Resolve competition among households, productive work, civic institutions, rural owners and authorities for valuable settlement ground. At City scale negotiate overlapping area-scale claims, land reservation, open space, development intensity and access across urban core and outskirts; at Street/district scale resolve actual parcels, tenure, subdivision, redevelopment and vertical development.
items.Observable effects: Area-scale concentrations emerge from work access, crowding and institutions: crowded low-capital quarters, spacious well-supported residential grounds, civic concentrations, commercial corridors and rural/fringe land under competing claims—not canned labels. Development pressure can cross a provisional urban outline or be resisted by farmland, old walls, public commons and physical barriers. At finer scale these patterns produce actual changes to parcels and premises.
items.Fields & products read: Inherited people/BuiltUp/Standing/ruins, crowding, wealth and work demand; the existing City stencil as a strong location prior; provisional typed district claims/programs and their spatial rights; existing land-use/tenure and cultural template rules, trade/access, waterways/terrain/hazards, cultivation, commons and defense; Street additionally reads actual parcels and occupancy.
items.Fields & products written: City-scale geographically coherent competing claims and resolved available/reserved land-use pressure, disputed/negotiated rights, density/intensification constraints and protection of commons/agriculture; no proprietary second population or built-stock fields. At Street scale, changed parcel geometry/use, subdivision, heights, negotiated entries and reuse rights through owners.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Competing claims operate on the canonical Town fabric and GIS geometry; offers and demand arrive through shared housing/institutional questions, not hard-coded city archetypes. Society density and property rights are contextual inputs, not created by subdivision.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: World/Region scarcity and constructed capital remain handled by existing society processes; City strategy resolves present area-scale land/rights competition for urban core, suburbs and supported rural satellites; Street strategy resolves local plots and buildings. Refinement adds no historical decades.
items.Other process interactions: City stencil strongly biases urban competition/development pressure inside, while actual claims for roadside commerce, agriculture, suburbs and outposts may extend beyond. Early typed districts compete for suitable land and shape ownership, spatial openness and development intensity before construction and major ways finalize; investment/defense and improved accessibility modify their viability. Resolved claims influence permanent district tessellation, but are not merely classifications.
items.Invariants / obligations: Claims must be traceable to inherited occupants, rights, sponsors, access, economy and material conditions; preserve public space, workable farmland and authored tenure. In City do not assume parcel geometry, enforce uniform district archetypes, or use district edges/core stencils as permission masks. In Street avoid subdivisions through built structures or beyond viable lots. Do not fabricate people, built capital or historical years.
items.Review notes: Owner correction: District primary type and selected template are generative inputs at City-scale, with strong stencil prior to urban land pressure. Do not flatten district identity into an economic gradient or turn the stencil into an absolute construction mask.

items.Semantic name: Shared services, institutions and pooled civic works
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Allow inhabitants, businesses and authorities to coordinate resources for common needs, operate institutions, maintain precincts and build collective infrastructure at supported locations.
items.Observable effects: Real funded institutions create legible multi-block civic/religious/administrative precincts, public squares, protected corridors and active approaches. When supported by threat, authority, wealth and terrain, defensive works form inner compounds, partial perimeters, retained old rings or later fortifications with functioning gates; many cities remain unwalled. A temple/library/court influences surrounding urban geometry rather than simply marking nearby blocks civic.
items.Fields & products read: Actual needs and existing civic/institutional promises, sponsors/household/enterprise support, inherited public power/tenure and resources, EARLY town.districts type programs whose eligible physical character implies civic/defensive needs, the City stencil and selected template rights/defensibility, candidate sites and external catchments, real threats, travel networks and independently grounded major-work/POI prerequisites.
items.Fields & products written: Justified civic and common-ground reservations, sponsor/ownership and service commitments, precinct extent/rights, commissioned or reused major works and public-space claims; explicitly proposed/funded defensive enclosures and gate/crossing requirements (including partial, inner, older and outer walls) sent to construction and movement for physical realization. Work ownership, use and support remain persistent, not an anonymous civic label.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Institutions speak benefits and prerequisites through the POI catalogue; shared question consumers value those benefits. Resource pooling, cultural practice and allegiance influence eligibility and funding without a type-specific rule embedded in every other process.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: City: spatially express inherited and supported institutional/defensive commitments as area-scale precinct rights, wall projects and public places during present-state refinement. Street/district: elaborate local institutional premises and services while inheriting City works. Do not replay history or invent new population/resources merely to build a City map.
items.Other process interactions: Early typed district programs can create legitimate demand for civic ground, sponsorship and enclosures where their actual occupants/institutions support it, while real patrons and template rights constrain what survives. Collective investment's precinct and defensive decisions feed spatial effects back to district identity, construction, movement and land competition BEFORE final City district polygons. Typology alone cannot create free palaces/temples/guards or unconstrained magical works.
items.Invariants / obligations: Every public work and fortified project needs operational purpose, legitimate sponsor or inherited identity, plausible budget/materials/support and a physically meaningful site. Defensive enclosure is optional, can be multiple or partial, cannot silently equate to the city edge and must not block all trade/access; retain old walls when outgrown. No automatic one-market-per-district or civic radius around a landmark; preserve authorship and established rights, including conflicts.
items.Review notes: Owner correction: City districts embody their chosen types. Investment must respond to their meaningful early civic/defensive program, without inventing patrons or merely decorating finished district polygons.

items.Semantic name: Urban landscape and detailed premises realization
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Spatially realize inherited developed land and city-stencil-conditioned strong urbanization into coherent, characterful City built intensity, institutions, open grounds, defended works, developed fringes and supported countryside sites. Read the selected template and active district programs as CAUSAL form instructions before City geometry is fixed. At Street/district fidelity, resolve detailed streets, blocks, premises and buildings from the authoritative City type/geometry.
items.Observable effects: Inside the City stencil, occupied developable land generally develops into a coherent, strongly built urban body or supported parks, commons, ceremonial grounds and other purposeful voids; districts express pronounced type-specific physical character. Outside the stencil development drops sharply but does not vanish: farmland, dispersed homes, clustered gate suburbs, waystations, markets, guardposts and settlements survive where trade, inhabitants and geography justify them. Walls where supported may enclose parts of the city while suburbs continue beyond.
items.Fields & products read: Existing City stencil (strong interior urbanization prior, nonzero outside potential), inherited Population/BuiltUp/Standing/ruins/food/trade and capital condition; live town.districts type programs/area claims and selected founding template; land-competition rights, civic/defense projects, routes/gates, terrain and resources, existing named structures, outside economic connections.
items.Fields & products written: City-scale connected developed-land patches/intensity, housing/work/civic land use, major precinct and landmark grounds, outlying farmsteads/hamlets/market stops/waystations/guardposts when supported, and persistent physical walls/fortifications and entrances for named/publication geometry. Street/district-scale local blocks, premises, yards, workshops and buildings. Any legitimate numeric feedback passes through society stock owner, without new inhabitants or fictitious historical years.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Use domain-owned developed stock as magnitude and form constraints, not a cell-by-cell footprint template. Street access enables development; land competition intensifies/reuses scarce sites; institutions reserve plazas, halls and grounds; trade and maintenance produce differing effective construction and occupation.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: City: resolve broad urban land, precincts, walls, suburban transitions and satellite/outlying supported features over main settlement plus City hinterland; no ordinary local block/plot/street generation. Street/district: refine inherited district and City land-use/route/works constraints into local streets, blocks, plots, buildings and occupation. World/Region built-stock patterns remain society-owned; child realization adds no historical epoch.
items.Other process interactions: Read active district type programs EARLY. The district role/physical signature influences construction intensity, development shape, open grounds, major precincts and defensibility in competition with actual capital, access and rights; construction feeds realized effects back into district program viability and later permanent partition. Cooperative investment sponsors meaningful walls/precincts and movement supplies gates/corridors. Separate City stencil preference from final district polygons, City map extent and physical enclosure.
items.Invariants / obligations: The City stencil is a STRONG spatial PRIOR, not a zero/one permission mask: support broadly continuous urbanization within viable stencil ground while reserving justified empty spaces; substantially lower development outside except for supported roads, suburbs, farming and discrete opportunities. Do not produce uniform built texture inside, decorate outside randomly or overwrite canonical numeric society stocks. Give each district's chosen type visible consequences at City scale before publishing geometry; no template-driven finished map stamping, additional historical time or mandatory wall.
items.Review notes: Owner correction supersedes prior overcorrection: KEEP the existing City stencil and make it strongly predictive of built-up development inside; only remove its behavior as an absolute exclusion for anything outside. Urban districts are active type-bearing drivers of City development, not labels assigned after construction.

items.Semantic name: Built-capital upkeep, deterioration and reuse
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Maintain, weather, repair, neglect or abandon constructed land and standing works using resources, exposure, institutions and physical damage across map scales; resolve the resulting condition spatially before individual buildings exist.
items.Observable effects: Well-funded centers can retain high standing and usable capacity, while chronically flooded neighborhoods, animal-invaded abandoned plots and battered settlements lose functional stock, and farmsteads persist with very different maintenance investment. Damage, repairs and ruins yield recognizable settlement mosaics without parcel drawings.
items.Fields & products read: Retained BuiltUp, Standing and ruins, occupation/crowding, trade wealth and labor, climate/water and storm exposure, ecological encroachment and animal impacts, magical preservation/corrosion/hazards, conflict damage, institutional services and actual elapsed time where applicable.
items.Fields & products written: Historically justified renewal or degradation of built capital, usable-capacity/condition state and ruined retained stock through the single society/built-land owner. Region strategy differentiates present condition of inherited stock by local causes, not new centuries of decay; City/Street can later resolve individual premises.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Multiple independent phenomena contribute through shared care, exposure, preservation, damage and investment questions: trade and human institutions fund repair; climate, hydrology, ecology/animals and magic alter durability; `human.land.meet` and sieges supply acute damage without duplicating the same loss.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: World: actual timed construction upkeep, weathering and neglect; Region: present spatial resolution of inherited functional versus ruined stock with iterative local condition/usage feedback. City/Street: finer building-level strategies, if relevant, not needed for the Region city pilot.
items.Other process interactions: Interacts with `human.land.harden` for construction/reuse, `human.land.gather` via functional capacity, `human.land.trade` via investment, `human.land.meet` via hazards and regional ecological/animal presence; later `town.construction` resolves details.
items.Invariants / obligations: No duplicate condition/ruin stock or automatic damage per refinement iteration. Unchanging inherited quality remains plausible; deterioration must have exposure, time or a legitimate present spatial differentiation source. No blanket 'more population = better buildings' rule.
items.Review notes: PROMOTE this existing semantic process beyond City/Street: use numeric built-land stock mechanisms in World and Region, and geometry only at later fidelity. Avoid creating a second `human.land.maintain` process. Reuse BuiltUp/Standing/ruins unless the pilot proves an additional shared condition/capacity field is necessary.

items.Semantic name: Local cultivation, field tenure and fallowing
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Resolve inherited and ongoing agricultural land use into fields, grazing areas, working access and fallow transitions in the settlement's actual terrain and economy.
items.Observable effects: Visible field strips, orchards, pastures and fallow parcels follow soils, water, paths and holdings. Active farms may expand, contract or shift as people, market access and settlement construction alter their viability.
items.Fields & products read: Parent-scale farmland/pasture shares and working history, actual soils/water/slope, roads, labor and cultivator premises, tenure, grazing pressure, water rights, boundary markets and physical planting constraints.
items.Fields & products written: Supported agricultural parcel geography and use, current worked/fallow state, worker-to-field relationships, productive access and the local land occupied by cultivation. Any change to macro food supply passes through the society/ecology owner.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Society owns broad agricultural occupation and food markets; local cultivation owns how that occupation manifests spatially and links to labor, drainage, trade and ecological land use. Crop and pasture success is not inferred merely from a polygon being drawn.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: City-edge/block and Street/field fidelity. Refinement spatially realizes inherited cultivation; additional working/fallow changes need explicit local causal exposure, not a repeat of world-century farm expansion.
items.Other process interactions: Movement opens fields; construction and land competition take land; livelihood supplies labor/markets; ecosystem and water conditions determine viable crops/pasture; publication retains plot identity.
items.Invariants / obligations: Do not conjure new food or people from an agricultural polygon. Preserve founded farms and inherited worked landscape where meaningful, respect water/building conflicts, and keep farmland/pasture and fallow distinctions visible.
items.Review notes: Semantic process spanning local agricultural realization and ordinary field use. Do not split its responsibility merely because geometry placement and worker assignment are implemented in different helpers.

items.Semantic name: Settlement GIS realization and publication
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Publish an established town's resolved physical and functional geography into authoritative map features without causing new settlement development.
items.Observable effects: Inspectable settlement entities, roads, footpaths, civic spaces, fields, wards, premises, buildings, addresses, major works and operational relations represent the retained town at the map's fidelity.
items.Fields & products read: Resolved Town fabric and retained settlement/POI identities, place naming and social attributes, canonical road/access graph, spatial frame, authored protection and chosen publication fidelity.
items.Fields & products written: Stable GIS feature IDs, located point/line/polygon geometry, networks, addresses, relationships, meaningful attributes and provenance. Does not create new population, shops, construction age or historical occupation.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Publication consumes the products of town, society and physical domains through a single GIS boundary; it uses shared feature schemas, spatial operations and ownership instead of becoming another generator.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: Finalization of a City or Street map's current developed state, or a deliberate re-publication after authorized change. No elapsed time or independent development pass.
items.Other process interactions: Consumes all preceding town mechanisms, inherited named works, cultivation and transport; GIS inspection/export/authoring consume its features. It cannot retrospectively change why a town exists.
items.Invariants / obligations: Stable entity and relationship identity, usable street/address topology, truthful attributes, no fabricated census, no mutation of generator-owned facts. Re-publication must preserve protected/authored map contents and avoid duplicate features.
items.Review notes: Non-process publication contract. It realizes existing retained town results; development remains owned by the phenomena that produced them.

items.Semantic name: Biological colonization and ecological origins
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Establish the first viable life, seed stocks and ecological succession potential where physical conditions and dispersal pathways permit; separate a true origin event from the realization of life already carried by a parent.
items.Observable effects: Newly hospitable ground receives pioneers, seed sources and initial food webs; contrasting soils, waterways, islands and climate leave distinct patterns of early colonization. Established forest and fauna persist when a map is viewed more closely.
items.Fields & products read: Available substrate and weathered soil, land/water/ice boundaries, warmth and moisture, paths for seed/animal arrival, inherited cover and seed banks, retained ecology history and any authored biological facts.
items.Fields & products written: Founded vegetation/seed cohorts, initial trophic populations and associated nutrient/soil stores only where the world genuinely begins life. For a child, resolved inherited cohorts and habitat occupancy without creating another founding generation.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Ground, hydrology and climate define viable establishment; transport carriers determine how propagules arrive, and system-specific magic modifies viability through its medium. Biological owner maintains living stocks and references actual environmental history.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: World-origin colonization at the genuine beginning of an ecosystem, with later recolonization only where a distinct causal event clears/opens ground. Refinement of Region/City/Street uses inherited ecological initial conditions and spatial realization, not a fresh historical origin.
items.Other process interactions: Supplies life to ecological succession and food webs; soil/erosion, glaciation, fire, Greenwood or Aurora can change colonizable ground; settlement and agriculture may later remove or encourage propagules.
items.Invariants / obligations: Do not reseed or regrow from scratch when changing resolution. Inherited forest, wetland, fauna and seed distributions must remain credible; source stocks and dispersal mechanisms bound what can colonize a previously empty place.
items.Review notes: Semantic ecological-establishment process; generic bootstrap, field compatibility and existing-state transfer belong to supporting contracts rather than new instances of this causal event.

items.Semantic name: Ecological succession and population dynamics
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Advance vegetation communities, soils, animal food webs and organic productivity through **actual elapsed environmental time**, including colonization, growth, competition, turnover, migration and natural disturbance.
items.Observable effects: Forests mature or retreat, grasslands and wetlands shift, soils recover or erode, grazing animals and predators occupy suitable habitats, and fires/floods leave real ecological scars. Old-growth, young stands and post-disturbance mosaics become distinct places.
items.Fields & products read: Existing living cohorts and seeds, fauna/prey/predator populations, soils/carbon, climatic seasonal forcing, water/ice/drainage, physical disturbance, magic-specific effects, environmental exchange across map boundaries and explicit elapsed duration.
items.Fields & products written: Living cover, species-group ages/seed banks, grazer/browser/predator/fish stocks, carbon/nutrient and soil states, dispersion and disturbance legacy; derived biome categories are produced by a separate interpretation contract.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Ecology couples through shared environmental and land-use questions with hydrology, climate, sediment, magic and society. Species move on their physical carriers; predators follow prey; living cover feeds back into infiltration, root strength and hillslope erosion.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: World historical/ecological epochs, with true duration and geographic dispersal reach. Child maps may elaborate current habitat through a distinct present-state strategy but do not advance the World lineage by another epoch.
items.Other process interactions: Receives pioneer stocks from ecological establishment, habitat suitability from environmental-response processes and anthropogenic disturbance from human land use. Feeds terrain stability, soil/water, magic's biological media, hunting/food and biome publication.
items.Invariants / obligations: Time-dependent mortality, maturation and nutrient turnover occur only when warranted by elapsed causal history. Preserve existing cohorts, seed sources and connectivity; no arbitrary cover patches or extra aging during pure refinement.
items.Review notes: Distinct semantic process from a current-state habitat response: succession describes how living communities change **over time**. It may share algorithms and scheduling implementations without sharing ownership of the phenomenon.

items.Semantic name: Ecological response to changed habitat conditions
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Adjust the **present ecological distribution and stress response** when relief, flooding, ice, climate, water chemistry, magical forcing or other habitat conditions change, without treating the redraw itself as new historical time.
items.Observable effects: River-margin wetlands find wetter hollows, forests retreat from newly exposed cliffs and coasts, thawed areas reveal plausible vegetation, salt or ice may suppress living cover, and local habitat diversity follows actual soil and water.
items.Fields & products read: Inherited living cover, cohorts, age and soil/seed context; current terrain and substrate, moisture/flow/flooding, seasonal climate, ice/water levels, disturbance evidence, named magic media and effects, protected ecological features; incoming/downstream connectivity.
items.Fields & products written: Conditioned present cover and ecological viability, localized stress/availability, redistribution or realization of suitable cohorts and animal habitats where justified. Avoid new historical carbon stock, new population age or repeated disaster mortality.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Reads the same shared physical and magical forcing used by ecological succession but responds to **what the environment now is**. Effects that truly require years of succession or a new disaster must be delegated to an elapsed process.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: Present-state physical response and refinement development at World/Region/City/Street when relevant geography changes. Local algorithms and resolution determine details; no duplicate epoch duration is bound to a child map.
items.Other process interactions: Couples with glacier/river/coastal refinement, soil and hydrology, Fire/Aurora/Greenwood/Salt/Pressure physical effects, land-use impacts and the inherited ecology. Supplies coherent habitats to food/web and classification.
items.Invariants / obligations: Preserve the ecological history inherited from a parent, keep system-specific consequences visible, and do not impose uniform biome substitutions. Re-applying response to unchanged conditions should not cumulatively kill organisms or invent centuries of recovery.
items.Review notes: Separate semantic responsibility from succession. Whether some behaviors are implemented by the same ecological engine is an implementation strategy, not evidence that the two meanings are identical.

items.Semantic name: Organic burial, exposure and geological maturation
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Carry accumulated living carbon into sedimentary deposits where actual burial occurs and let retained organic layers mature or be exhumed through geological exposure and heating.
items.Observable effects: Peat basins, buried forests, carbon-rich deltas, fossil-fuel provinces and exhumed organic horizons reflect the world's sedimentary and thermal history. Wetlands and high-productivity coastlines leave distinguishable subsurface legacies.
items.Fields & products read: Peat, soil and aquatic organic carbon, sediment deposition/erosion, retained burial depth/material affiliation, rock-column transport and temperature/geothermal exposure over real geological time.
items.Fields & products written: Retained buried organic materials and provenance, burial depth and maturity, converted coal/oil/gas stores when supported, reduced or re-exposed surface organic reserves. Separate ecological/stratigraphic identity must survive changes of cover.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Ecology supplies biomass; physical deposition, erosion and crust transport supply the actual burial/exhumation mechanism; geothermal energy and duration control maturation. Magical preservation changes decay through its medium, not by declaring a magical fossil-fuel type.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: Multi-epoch geological time on World history; relevant finer maps inherit layered deposits and may reveal their structure without replaying burial or millions of years of maturation.
items.Other process interactions: Follows vegetation/animal productivity and organic carbon accumulation; interacts with sediment routing, tectonics, heat history, Salt and Greenwood media, resource sites and present terrain exposure.
items.Invariants / obligations: No buried resource without corresponding organic stock, physical deposition and age/thermal conditions. Preserve provenance and finite stores; a newly refined or classified map must not repeatedly bury the same peat or generate fresh fossil deposits.
items.Review notes: Semantic process; record keeping, final ecological normalization and publication are not part of organic burial merely because they may follow it in the causal schedule.

items.Semantic name: Ecological state reconciliation
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Reconcile retained living state and derived aggregate quantities at a process boundary so consumers see a coherent current ecosystem, without enacting a new ecological event.
items.Observable effects: Canopy totals, vegetation-group shares, state constraints and derived indicators agree with the living stocks; the map remains ready for downstream ecological questions and publication, without an independent new forest or mortality event.
items.Fields & products read: Latest authoritative living cohorts, ecological constraints and source identity, current environmental conditions and authored protections; relevant completed state changes from true ecological processes.
items.Fields & products written: Consistent derived canopy and cohort totals, normalized/readable ecological state and invalidated/recomputed caches. No new biomass, casualties, carbon deposits, years of growth or independent biome history.
items.Shared questions / coupling: State-finalization contract within ecology's writer; classification and GIS publication are separate. Physical and magical changes needing actual biological effects belong to response/succession processes, not housekeeping.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: At selected execution/commit boundaries for World and refined maps. It is a state operation, not an elapsed year, biological generation round or historical epoch.
items.Other process interactions: Follows establishment, succession, environmental response and organic burial; supplies consistent state to habitat queries, society, magic and biome classification.
items.Invariants / obligations: Idempotent on unchanged input; cannot create, kill, age or transport organisms. Preserve inherited/authored state and distinguish causal change from data normalization.
items.Review notes: Non-process state finalizer. Keep mortality, stress and growth under their appropriate semantic processes, regardless of the filename or wrapper that currently triggers them.

items.Semantic name: Present-day biome and landscape classification
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Interpret an established ecosystem and its physical/magical forcing into recognizable habitat classes and map-facing landscape descriptions, without changing biological state.
items.Observable effects: Recognizable tundra, deserts, forests, grasslands, marshes, swamps, magical Ember groves, Rime forests, Fog heath, Deepwoods, Barrow heath, Salt pans and Glass flats appear where their distinct causal conditions are met.
items.Fields & products read: Current ground cover and vegetation cohorts, water and ice, weather/temperature/moisture, soil/carbon and system-specific Quickening, Stillness, fog, Verdure and Salting fields; geographic significance and existing named biome identities.
items.Fields & products written: Derived biome categories/coverage and diagnostic reasons for classifications; qualified landscape feature candidates for a separate GIS publication step. No new plants, magical stock, or geological morphology.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Classifier reads distinct underlying media and shared ecological/physical facts; multiple coexisting cover/forces remain available even if one surface class is selected. Significance governs which classified areas receive names, not whether a physical effect exists.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: Repeatable current-state interpretation at every map type/resolution where ecology is represented. It is independent of historical time, material transport and city-development rounds.
items.Other process interactions: Consumes present ecological response, succession, hydrology and the seven systems; feeds map legend, ecology-region extraction and sites without founding an ecosystem or destroying competing cover.
items.Invariants / obligations: Classes must reflect genuine physical and magical causes, especially distinct Salt and Fire/Aurora/Pressure/Greenwood effects; never replace underlying continuous fields with a single categorical scalar. Idempotent, no changes to organism stocks or named feature identities.
items.Review notes: Non-process classifier/derived-state contract. Lore names and landscape signatures are semantic requirements even if a particular classifier's current algorithm does not express all of them.

items.Semantic name: Human land-use impacts on ecosystems
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Model how cultivation, clearing, grazing, hunting, fishing, settlements and managed land alter ecosystems through **actual human history**, with ecological recovery and depletion feeding back into future society.
items.Observable effects: Cleared farmland opens forest, sustained herding produces grazed mosaics, heavy hunting/fishing depletes game, abandonment permits secondary growth, and long-lived institutions or protected groves leave alternative patterns. Different economies transform the same biome differently.
items.Fields & products read: Retained land use and settlement footprint, shared society questions for cleared/grazed/hunted/fished pressure, real historical duration and population activity, vegetation/seed and wildlife stocks, water/soil, access to outside stocks and magic-specific conditions.
items.Fields & products written: Ecologically supported changes to plant cover, nutrient/soil and carbon state, grazer/browser/fish populations, recovery and damage history. Does not directly alter society population or declare abstract 'cultivated' biomes without physical consequences.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Society contributes actual pressure and land-management practices through typed shared questions; ecology alone owns how vegetation, prey and soil respond. Magical craft changes ordinary rules only through the media/questions where its people practice it.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: Only genuine World human eras or other explicitly historical exposure with owned duration and land-use state. A child Region/City/Street inherits those consequences and realizes their finer spatial pattern; it does not redo decades of hunting or clearing.
items.Other process interactions: Interacts with society farming, food provision and trade, livelihood, ecosystem succession, plant/animal dispersal, soil water, fire risk and relevant Greenwood/Salt/Hallowed ecological effects.
items.Invariants / obligations: Depletion, recovery and abandonment require supported causal exposure, rather than a flat penalty for the presence of humans. Wildlife and crops use real carriers and boundary support; no repeated historic loss when refined or merely published.
items.Review notes: Keep historical land-use impacts as an ecology process. For Region refinement, current vegetation, wildlife, pests, rooting/encroachment and land cover can provide differentiated physical pressures on built-capital maintenance without replaying historical clearing, hunting or ecological succession; ecology and human layers remain separate owners.

items.Semantic name: Magical initial-state inheritance and realization
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Establish a map's configured seven-system state from its world origin or pinned parent: source identities, medium-bound inventories, reservoirs, confluence/door context and latent finer detail. This prepares initial conditions, not another episode of magical creation.
items.Observable effects: A new World has a coherent configured baseline from which sources can arise; a refined map reveals physically plausible positions and distributions of inherited Fire cores, Aurora charge, Pressure rays, Greenwood, Salt, Veil and Hallowed without duplicating their origins.
items.Fields & products read: Enabled-system configuration, original source identities and permissions, captured parent material stocks and spatial fields, rock/ice/water/vegetation/settlement media, map footprint and physical resolution, named places and historical provenance.
items.Fields & products written: Initialized typed magic reservoirs and origin associations, inherited source context, locally resolved distribution of available stocks and durable connections; no newly produced historical supply, elapsed depletion or automatic confluence event.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Per-system medium/inventory owners and inheritance providers; derived local distribution must reflect actual rock, water, ice, living cover and human maintenance, rather than copy one undifferentiated magic-intensity field.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: One-time map creation and restoration at World, Region, City or Street as applicable. World baseline may be empty; child resolution adds spatial detail to the completed present, with no historical duration.
items.Other process interactions: Prepares the starting context for medium-specific source supply, propagation, confluences, climate/rock/coastal coupling, history and publication. Authored or named sources remain independently identified.
items.Invariants / obligations: No duplicate origin, replenished finite stock, fabricated practitioner or new historical event merely because the map was refined. Material stays with its rightful medium and provenance; missing/disabled systems remain absent.
items.Review notes: Non-process state-realization contract spanning both captured-state transfer and finer spatial interpretation. Source formation, renewal and transport belong to the corresponding semantic magic processes.

items.Semantic name: Magical forcing of climate, water and weather
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Couple active, medium-specific magic effects into atmospheric and hydrological evolution: geothermal heat, ice-borne cold, deep-water Pressure rays and wakes, living-water influences, Salt desiccation, Hallowed deflection and causal confluences.
items.Observable effects: Fire produces thaw margins and warmer downstream water; Aurora leaves cold shadows and persistent ice; Pressure makes upwelling, coastal fog, storm tracks and sheltered rain shadows; other systems shape locally distinctive moisture and hazard gradients.
items.Fields & products read: Per-system active and stored stocks, source/medium geometry, existing temperature, wind, water and ice, ocean depth/current and coastal exposure, terrain relief, actual historical phase or present-state context, and relevant external forcing.
items.Fields & products written: Typed heat/cold, sea-temperature, fog, storm, moisture, evaporation, ice-retention and hydrological forcing made available to the physical owners. Changes to magical reservoirs are owned by source/transport processes, not generic climate projection.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Atmosphere, ocean, runoff, glacier and ecosystem processes consume named shared questions and source-specific effects; existing climate machinery resolves the resulting weather. Systems must never cancel by netting all magic onto one scalar.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: World historical climate stages when real time and stock changes occur; present-state conditioning for Region/City/Street where local relief, coasts and ice reveal finer consequences. Atmospheric reach may extend beyond the selected footprint.
items.Other process interactions: Receives source propagation and confluence forcing; affects drainage, coastal morphology, ice, vegetation, settlements and subsequent magical feedback. Rock/material changes remain separate receivers of the same specific causes.
items.Invariants / obligations: No effect without an active source, appropriate carrier or valid receiving medium. Distinct Fire, Aurora, Pressure and other mechanisms must remain recognizable; refinement refreshes current forcing without rerunning historical supply.
items.Review notes: A cross-domain *climate coupling stage*, not one generic 'magic-weather' phenomenon. Give each system's contributing effects first-class semantic ownership; the stage composes them into physical receivers.

items.Semantic name: Magical alteration of rock and retained materials
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Make the geological consequences of the seven systems physically real through their own media: Fire opens/heats/hardens conduits; Aurora alters ice-exposed rock; Pressure stresses coasts; Salt precipitates, fuses and domes; Greenwood changes soils/springs; Veil strains land; Hallowed restricts and displaces harm.
items.Observable effects: Conduit-altered bedrock, fractured thermal rims, crushed coasts, glass flats, sinkholes, disturbed Veil ground and long-lived stabilized ward interiors bear distinguishable material histories, even after the original active field has weakened.
items.Fields & products read: Rock columns, fractures, material resistance and burial, current magic stocks and carriers, tectonic/thermal stresses, ice and groundwater, shoreline/shelf geometry, original deposit provenance and actual geological or present forcing.
items.Fields & products written: Ground-owned structural/alteration state, fracture changes, rock resistance and physical hazard forcing; actual transported or deposited magical material stays associated with its proper host, depth and causal history.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Specific magical material mechanisms use the existing ground modes and geological questions; tectonics, erosion, weathering, ice and water can then transport or expose the resulting materials. Ecology or settlement read the changed land instead of a generic magical landform label.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: During genuine World geological changes, with local current-state material response where a real source/receiver changes. Finer maps resolve inherited stratigraphy and structures without adding a second ancient alteration history.
items.Other process interactions: Shares causes with source activity and climate/post-glacial coupling; feeds volcanic/fracture development, coast and slope processes, soil, magic-specific landscapes, ore deposits and later habitation.
items.Invariants / obligations: Respect rock/material ownership and host strata; never create mass, alteration or depth history solely to match an intensity color. Hallowed's displaced effects require a valid receiver; preserved geological consequences must survive source exhaustion and refinement.
items.Review notes: The registered label groups **several different material-response phenomena**. The process catalog should ultimately identify system-specific rock interactions and confluences, while this entry can own their physical coupling/selection boundary.

items.Semantic name: Late-stage magic propagation and confluence coupling
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Coordinate current magical supply, medium-bound transport, water exchange, terrain/ice responses and meetings once the relevant water, ice and coastal geography is available. 'Post-glacial' is a causal schedule position, not an eighth magic system or independent physical force.
items.Observable effects: Relict Aurora cold and moraines, Fire-warmed rivers, Pressure-exposed coasts, Greenwood spring corridors, Salt in dry basins, Hallowed kept roads, Veil doors and their distinctive meeting fronts develop as interacting consequences—not arbitrary pasted anomaly patches.
items.Fields & products read: Current water/ice/shoreline/drainage/ground state, each system's retained reservoirs and actual origins, prior climate forcing and medium transport, society-maintained routes or death history, named confluence definitions and legitimate elapsed exposure.
items.Fields & products written: A coherent set of system-owned source/transport/meeting effects, updated material and water forcing, source exhaustion/renewal where truly elapsed, and corresponding door/ward state; not a generic scalar called post-glacial magic.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Causally orders distinct source renewal, water/rock transport, live system effects and named confluences. Each system keeps its own medium and stocks; shared physics and landscape questions carry its consequences into other processes.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: World historical late-epoch stage with real elapsed time; at finer map types the equivalent work is **present-state realization and response only**. No repetition of centuries of magical accumulation, death records, material loss or door history.
items.Other process interactions: Composes source formation and exchange, magical climate/rock responses, hydrology, ice, society's routes and maintenance, confluences and classification. Its results may form new local detail only when inherited cause/context supports it.
items.Invariants / obligations: No supply without an eligible source, no duplicate Salt origin from an already-consumed death/lake record, no Veil door without stable supported ends, and no ward that simply deletes displaced effects. Preserve named and exhausted sources across scales.
items.Review notes: A *causal phase orchestrator* with substantive effects executed by the mechanisms it coordinates. The processes it composes—seven systems and their confluences—need independent semantic ownership; a stage is not itself a single magic phenomenon.

items.Semantic name: Current magical landscapes and confluence classification
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Interpret the current material stocks, effects and meetings as map-scale magical classes, coverage shares, signatures and candidate places. Classification reports magic's consequences; it does not generate or consume magical stock.
items.Observable effects: Distinct Fire veins/Ember groves, Aurora frozen zones, Pressure fog/crush coasts, Greenwood Deepwoods, Salt Barrow heaths and glass flats, Veil doors/wild zones, Hallowed wards and named interference fronts become legible at the appropriate scale.
items.Fields & products read: Per-system stored/active quantities and medium distributions, confluence strain/coverage, physical and ecological conditions, source and named landmark identities, map resolution and geographic significance rules.
items.Fields & products written: Derived class/coverage and feature-candidate descriptors with traceable system, origin and interaction semantics; underlying continuous fields and material histories remain unchanged.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Classifier reads independent system/media owners and natural environmental bands. Multiple systems may occupy shares of the same cell; significance governs naming, never the existence of an underlying physical effect.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: Repeatable current-state interpretation at every applicable map type and physical resolution; no elapsed years, source recharge, new weather or tectonic response.
items.Other process interactions: Follows source, climate, geological, ecological and confluence processes; informs magic GIS publication, ecological biome presentation, significance screening and place inspection.
items.Invariants / obligations: No winner-takes-all loss of overlapping stock, no generic 'magic-touched' class replacing distinct cause, and no duplicated named entity for a finer sample. Classification must not mutate the world.
items.Review notes: Classifier/derived-state contract only. The visible signatures are requirements rooted in the lore, but their physical causes belong to source, response and confluence processes.

items.Semantic name: Magic-to-coast forcing and boundary context
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Supply coast, shelf and marine processes with the present, spatially located influences of magical media and their meetings, so the ordinary coastal mechanisms—not a parallel magic-coast engine—shape erosion, water, fog, breaches and deposition.
items.Observable effects: Pressure-facing shores may crush or retreat, warm wakes and Fire vents alter nearby water, Aurora can hold an icy edge, Salt can accumulate in embayments, and Hallowed boundaries protect interiors while transferring burdens to exposed rims.
items.Fields & products read: Current coasts, bathymetry, ocean currents/waves, ice, shoreline geometry, incoming offshore rays and storms, current magical stocks/forcing, coastal material properties and ward/confluence footprints.
items.Fields & products written: Typed coastal forcing/context—stress, heat/cold, wave/upwelling exposure, brine transport, ward deflection and meeting hazards—for use by coastal and marine process owners. No independent coastal geometry or duplicate magic stock.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Boundary provider resolves outside-footprint incoming ocean and weather context; shoreline-dependent queries refresh after local geography changes. The existing coastal, water and material processes consume the shared forcing.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: Whenever a World or refined coastal map develops or refreshes its present shoreline; influence reaches outside the computational footprint. No historical storm or magical origin is replayed simply to evaluate a new coast.
items.Other process interactions: Consumes Fire/Aurora/Pressure/Salt/Hallowed and relevant confluences; affects marine circulation, coastal erosion, beach and delta deposition, ecological shore habitats, settlements and route hazards.
items.Invariants / obligations: Forcing must follow actual media and current coast geometry, not stale inherited shore coordinates. Offshore sources and deflected effects need real boundary receivers. The coastline owner retains the sole authority to change coast geometry.
items.Review notes: Domain-context and coupling provider, not a second coastal erosion process. Its contract must specify incoming/outgoing boundary influences as well as local on-map effects.

items.Semantic name: Magical source, stock and confluence provenance
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Retain causal evidence of genuine historical magical changes—source births and exhaustion, reservoir movement, medium interactions, confluences, material transformations and remembered sites—for explanation and later spatial realization.
items.Observable effects: Spent Fire ore and abandoned hearth towns, old Aurora-chilled valleys, Salt battlefields and dead basins, retired ward lines, broken door roads and altered rock can remain intelligible long after their active magical causes fade.
items.Fields & products read: Actual completed epoch outcomes, source and material lineage, reservoir changes, transport and alteration, named confluence and site identities, historical time/ancestry, and relevant recorded human maintenance or deaths.
items.Fields & products written: Provenance/history entries linking causes to source and place identities, past material/interaction state and true epoch relationships; observational history, not a substitute for retained physical stocks.
items.Shared questions / coupling: System-specific source and transport processes supply events; recorders retain their evidence. Child-map providers read completed history to realize geography; current-state queries must not infer or enact elapsed work.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: At actual World historical boundaries and other explicitly historical events. A Region/City/Street inherits selected provenance as pinned context, without appending a fake new age merely from refinement.
items.Other process interactions: Supports source life cycles, deep material histories, ecological and settlement consequences, place causality and map inspection; it cannot replace the authoritative current medium state.
items.Invariants / obligations: Recording must not create, charge, renew, move, kill or classify sources. Do not recount the same death/lake event as a second Salt origin or rewrite a named historical site when a child map adds detail.
items.Review notes: Non-process history/provenance recorder. It preserves enough specific origins, media and events to explain the present; the physical and magical processes alone cause the history.

items.Semantic name: Magical GIS and field publication
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Publish typed current magical fields, meaningful source/meeting sites, coverage and physical signatures into finished map/GIS representations so creators can inspect and use the results without invoking or changing generation.
items.Observable effects: Readers can find named Fire veins, Aurora crystals/ice fields, Pressure tracks, Greenwood springs, Salt pans, Hallowed sanctuaries, Veil doors and distinct interference hazards, with meaningful location and causal explanation.
