items.Fields & products read: Completed per-system material and intensity fields, classification/coverage, qualifying source and place identities, confluence records, accepted GIS/POI significance rules and persistent geographic coordinates.
items.Fields & products written: Stable GIS features and relationships, current typed magic channels, source/interaction attributes, bounded footprints and inspection/provenance links. Private stock/working state is not modified.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Consumes the magic classifier and existing place/feature catalogue; respects source and confluence identities, coexisting coverage shares and map-owned publication. Finished GIS readers should not need live generation inputs.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: Once per completed publication/commit at World, Region, City or Street where a magical phenomenon is meaningful. Geographic significance depends on map scale, not on whether the underlying force exists.
items.Other process interactions: Publishes outcomes of all seven media and their confluences alongside geology, ecology, society and settlement layers; Veil connections link appropriate real destinations, not just decorative icons.
items.Invariants / obligations: Never advance time, spawn sources, consume stocks or rewrite authored GIS. Retain stable names/identity, avoid promoting every microscopic trace to a named site, and do not flatten several systems into one output layer.
items.Review notes: Non-process publisher. Geographic realization is limited to representing **already established causes and identities**; any newly consequential physical effect must be produced upstream.

items.Semantic name: Persistent landmark emergence and physically supported emplacement
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Locate and establish persistent major landmarks at their historical emergence, applying their initial effects to the land.
items.Observable effects: A distinctive mountain, escarpment, waterfall, canyon, crater, dome, stone ring or magic-shaped feature emerges at a legible site with a form and lasting consequences. Its position reflects what formed it, and notable features can acquire identity and stories across epochs.
items.Fields & products read: Current tectonics, rock/material layers, rivers and coast, geological events and past damage, stable/latent landmark roster and ID, landscape suitability, relevant magic stock/charge and temporal source activity, named/authored landmark constraints and parent evidence.
items.Fields & products written: Retained landmark identity, emplacement epoch and site/extent, measurable form/effect targets and causal history, recorded physical changes only when the landmark type actually has a distinct material/energy action, and later GIS realization/latent support.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Landmark catalog and site suitability select the phenomenon; rock, water and magic owners execute causal changes through shared modes, ledger and source media. Recognition of a pre-existing natural formation is not license to sculpt it twice.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: At true historical emergence on a World, or at a supported actual new event; Region/City/Street refinement realizes inherited/latent landmark form without a second emplacement or a new ancient event. Preserve its spatial influence outside the visible footprint.
items.Other process interactions: Works with mountain building, faulting, impacts, erosion, river falls, magic confluences, ecological change and human significance. Maintenance and local place publication subsequently update form and consequences.
items.Invariants / obligations: Requires credible formation evidence and site/medium suitability, with stable named identity and no accidental duplicate event or material budget. If too small to realize on coarse cells, retain latent causes and identity; authored landmarks remain authoritative where provided.
items.Review notes: One landmark-emergence responsibility spanning selection, effects and identity. A geographic label alone is not an emplacement; a physically acting landmark must consume/contribute material and energy through the relevant owner.

items.Semantic name: Landmark persistence, alteration and loss through history
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Maintain and update established landmarks through later history, responding to changes in their physical surroundings.
items.Observable effects: Major landscape signatures can resist weathering, be cut back, widened, submerged, reactivated or decay; old fractures, rings, domes, gorges and ritual effects leave recognizable, sometimes ruined remnants rather than disappearing at the next epoch.
items.Fields & products read: Established landmark ID, original extent/causes, retained geomorphic and material measures, epoch history and elapsed stress, current erosion/deposition/water/ice/magic forces, changed sites and source availability, inherited regional and outside-footprint context.
items.Fields & products written: Updated landmark persistence, measured shape, strength, exposure, damage/recovery and event notes; any material-backed maintenance or deterioration effects through actual Ground, water or magic owner operations. Named identity and ancestry persist even if active expression changes.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Landmark owner compares physical state to its historically credible form and applies only supported ongoing forces; material/ecological/magical owners retain their budgets. It does not restore an arbitrary target height or maintain a dead magical effect by decree.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: Across later real World epochs and genuine continuing local present processes; children remeasure established features without repeating past alteration. Active maintenance only where a real source and elapsed time exist.
items.Other process interactions: Coupled to tectonic reactivation, erosion, mass wasting, sea changes, ice, magical charge and human protection/use; revises historical accounts and publication status as forms change or survive.
items.Invariants / obligations: An old feature must remain historically traceable even when damaged; no regeneration of vanished mass or perpetual invariance from a remembered target alone. Remeasurement and public presentation are read-only and distinct from physical evolution.
items.Review notes: Maintenance is a conditional causal process; distinguish measuring the landmark's current signature from acting on it, and define failure/ruin as valid historical outcomes.

items.Semantic name: Real-scale channel pool and riffle realization
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Locate and publish pools along water channels at their real physical dimensions.
items.Observable effects: Deeper quiet pools at low-gradient stretches, confluences and outer bends alternate with shallower riffles and rapids; local fishing, wading and route choices reflect true channel dimensions and flow instead of stylized river-line thickness.
items.Fields & products read: Retained channel reach, water width/depth and discharge, longitudinal bed gradient and bend/confluence geometry, erosion/deposition evidence, parent river continuity, downstream/incoming context, already recognized named pools.
items.Fields & products written: Situated pool outlines and water-depth/flow descriptors as local geographic features, with reach linkage and causal evidence. Any actual bed scour is owned by the river/erosion process; no additional unaccounted excavation or water volume.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Real-scale interpreter uses channel hydraulics and bed geometry to realize pools, with separate GIS publication. Local river reaches and banks retain identity; standing water/meltwater supply comes from the water owner.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: City/Street or other sufficiently fine physical resolution where a pool can be represented at true size; never require every map type to create individual pools. No elapsed new fluvial history when placing pool geometry.
items.Other process interactions: Receives river channel geometry, sediment transport, bank material and tributary junctions; informs fishing habitat, settlement access, fords and waterfalls/other place recognition.
items.Invariants / obligations: A pool must fit a connected river with plausible depth, hydraulic cause and real dimensions; avoid decorative pools at constant-grade reaches. Same parent river may reveal more pools at finer fidelity without duplicating older excavation.
items.Review notes: Real-scale derived morphology/feature realization, not an independent river erosion epoch. Keep GIS drawing downstream from hydraulic state.

items.Semantic name: Rock outcrop, bare slope and cliff exposure realization
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Expose and publish visible rock outcrops and cliffs from the local material and terrain.
items.Observable effects: Cliffs, ledges and bedrock outcrops emerge at the correct faces where steep gradients, cut banks, thin soils or weathered material expose rock; different material families produce distinct visible surfaces and local obstacles.
items.Fields & products read: Current Ground rock columns and exposed faces, bedrock depth/rock resistance, soil/colluvium and sediment cover, slope and erosion history, water and weathering context, inherited cliff/outcrop IDs and real-scale ground geometry.
items.Fields & products written: Real-scale exposed-rock and cliff footprints with material type, face and observable evidence, published as geographic geology features. No generated new bedrock, erosion or synthetic mineral deposit.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Read-only material/exposure interpreter asks Ground and slopes, while geological processes own rock formation and wear. GIS publisher maps the resulting true-size surfaces and respects authored feature ownership.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: Present World/Region/City/Street where the physical resolution permits credible outcrop geometry (usually fine City/Street); parent outcrops can be detailed without changing the time state.
items.Other process interactions: Interacts with tectonic cliff formation, glacial scars, stream incision, mass wasting and soil cover. Influences travel costs, habitat, quarry sites, landmark recognition and local construction.
items.Invariants / obligations: Outcrop existence and kind must agree with actual stratigraphy and cover; no visible rock hovering above uncut soil or different rock type from the underlying column. Preserve inherited prominent cliffs rather than redetecting unrelated ones.
items.Review notes: Physical landscape realization/publication contract. Exposed rock is evidence of a previous mechanism, not a second rock-generation process.

items.Semantic name: Demand-driven foot-trail emergence and wear
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Connect otherwise unserved destinations to existing local ways with traversable trails.
items.Observable effects: Repeated travel from destinations to existing ways leaves traversable tracks that bend around cliffs, wetlands and deep water; shortcuts join into an evolving local footpath network with more wear on shared segments.
items.Fields & products read: Visited and socially meaningful places (including outside-boundary destinations), existing paths, streets, highway/crossing network, travel cost from real slope/water/vegetation/risks, actual passage demand and retained parent path identities.
items.Fields & products written: New or strengthened local trail courses, use/wear and connection state with stable route references, plus publishable real-scale line geometry; no automatically commissioned road, bridge or populated place.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Society, settlement and travel owners supply actual demand and established ways; physical and magical fields supply traversal costs, and the route owner writes path-wear/connectivity. The later GIS publisher is not the mechanism.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: Present repeated-use or local development process at fine physical resolution, particularly Street and detailed City. A child realizes the routes serving a wider travel network; do not generate history-free trails solely because a point appears in a crop.
items.Other process interactions: Connects camps, springs, landmarks, homes and markets to existing ways; crossings, river width, slope and hazards determine access; repeated shared journeys can concentrate wear into lanes while abandonment fades paths.
items.Invariants / obligations: A trail must have a reachable origin/destination and physically valid traversability, with explicit external connections. Avoid double-adding inherited paths and inventing bridges or roads; changes to established routes need causes such as use, erosion or loss.
items.Review notes: Genuine access-network mechanism despite current real-scale registration under publication. Publication is the final output of socially supported path wear, not its semantic owner.

items.Semantic name: Ford and bridge recognition at water-route intersections
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Resolve fords and bridges wherever local routes intersect water channels.
items.Observable effects: Travel routes meet channels at viable fords, maintained bridges or impediments. Shallow streams can be waded; deeper crossings require established works and supporting approaches, making rivers useful geographic barriers rather than ordinary map lines.
items.Fields & products read: Established footpaths/roads and water routes, true river widths, depth, discharge and flood/seasonal levels, bank/abutment terrain, inherited authored and named crossing sites, existing bridge/ford infrastructure and local work/maintenance evidence.
items.Fields & products written: Crossing location and type, route/water and infrastructure links, true-size bridge/ford geometry where supported, and accessibility effects. No newly constructed bridge or changed river channel without a corresponding actual construction/engineering process.
items.Shared questions / coupling: The water owner supplies physical feasibility and passage costs; settlement/works or known paths supply existing engineered crossings. A recognition and access-coupling step may propose a crossing, but bridge construction is a distinct social/engineering cause.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: Present geographic realization on fine City/Street or any map of sufficient physical resolution; inherit parent known bridges and fords and reconcile with refined shore geometry. No replay of centuries of bridge building.
items.Other process interactions: Couples trail and road networks to channel hydraulics, flood risk, local institutions, dams and river transport. An absent/failed crossing may create a diversion, ferry or a barrier with social consequences.
items.Invariants / obligations: No bridge merely because two GIS strokes overlap; a true ford must be shallow/passable in its intended season, and a bridge needs physical support and construction provenance. Preserve crossing identity, external route continuity and real dimensions.
items.Review notes: Coupling/realization contract for crossings rather than an automatic bridge-builder; distinguish recognizing a crossing from causing an engineered crossing.

items.Semantic name: Individual vegetation, stones and ground-detail realization
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Realize individual plants, rocks and small ground-cover details from the underlying ecology and material state at visible resolution.
items.Observable effects: Small map spaces reveal recognizable trees, reeds, shrubs, loose stones, deadwood and other locally grounded detail at realistic spacing and size, with open clearings, wet patches and rocky surfaces rather than uniform decorative scatter.
items.Fields & products read: Retained grass/tree/wetland cover and ecological cohort history, plant groups and seed/age density, soil depth/rock and sediment, wetness, water/ice exposure, land use and built footprints, inherited important objects and real-sized object catalogue.
items.Fields & products written: Individually located and sized visible vegetation/stone/ground objects with stable geographic placement where needed; no new ecological biomass, geologic formation or sediment volume. True-scale objects are published through the GIS/object owner.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Spatial realization samples physical cover shares into discrete manifestations appropriate to fidelity, while ecology and Ground retain actual density/material ownership. Avoid converting every abstract cover percentage into a permanent named object.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: Only when World/Region/City/Street physical resolution can genuinely show individual objects (normally fine City/Street). Finer rerendering refines positions, sizes and composition from parent captures without replaying growth or rock weathering.
items.Other process interactions: Receives ecological succession, land use, water/soil wetness, rocks/landslides, atmospheric conditions, settlements and trails; revealed objects influence local travel, visibility, resource gathering and site texture.
items.Invariants / obligations: Expected density and size ranges should match real biomass/rock exposure, occupied ground and habitat; objects cannot appear through buildings, deep water or impossible surfaces. Maintain significant persistent tree/rock IDs, while ordinary scatter remains derived detail.
items.Review notes: Real-scale ecological/geologic detail realization, not another vegetation- or rock-growing process. Output is inspectable objects, not new physical history.

items.Semantic name: Society land-pass orchestration
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: Coordinate actual World social history over elapsed eras and registered processes, without representing the nonhistorical spatial-refinement iterations as additional eras.
items.Observable effects: Coordinates one human era's sequence of population founding, craft learning, trade, feeding, demographic change, movement, construction and aging.
items.Fields & products read: Configured human-era duration/mobility, current society state, travel and process questions.
items.Fields & products written: No distinct semantic state; delegates writes to the invoked society processes and owner operations.
items.Shared questions / coupling: Calls `human.land.pass` repeatedly; resolves food, goods, settlement, craft and human-owner participants in a deliberate order.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: World history only: arrange historical migration, food, trade, demographic, construction, culture and political events over genuine elapsed time. A distinct refinement scheduler invokes the same processes' scale-specific spatial strategies without elapsed eras.
items.Other process interactions: Interleaves food markets, growth, migration and construction; participates in broader culture/realm and ecology era sequencing.
items.Invariants / obligations: Do not call elapsed demographic, hunger, trade-wear or construction-aging operations from the Region/City spatial solver. Keep independent scheduling and dependency validation for World historical and child spatial execution.
items.Review notes: Retain as history orchestration only; do not create another generic 'society growth' process or reuse its `Facts::settled(years)` with fabricated historical duration to refine space.

items.Fields & products read: Strong City stencil/envelope prior from the city map's captured settled outline or supported region/settlement morphology; inherited Population, BuiltUp, Standing, occupation/crowding/wealth/maintenance, external access, terrain/water, selected founding template and its City/district-level rules, institutional/POI/major-work sites, physical/magical context, tenure/land claims, routes, defense/walls/gates, authored district identities, public/open-land claims.
items.Fields & products written: Before other City geometry settles: persistent provisional district programs—primary distinctive type/role, eligible site/anchor, character rules, intended spatial signature, claims/pressures/reservations and interactions—that actively guide movement, land-competition, collective investment and construction. After coupled resolution: 7–14 durable typed district identities, complete authoritative polygons of the main stencil-influenced urban body, explicit internal meaningful open areas, adjacency, rights/access and inherited district-development guidance. NOT a development clip or independently owned census/BuiltUp/Standing.
items.Invariants / obligations: Each active district has a meaningful dominant program with physical City-scale consequences; do not assign type after all geometry is drawn or dilute types into undifferentiated average scores. Types must be eligible from actual template/site/history/economy/institution/wealth evidence; exaggerated stylization may amplify contrast but not conjure unsupported monarchies, temples, magical devices or workforces. Use the City stencil as a STRONG development/organization prior inside, not a hard prohibition outside; respect authored facts. Final 7–14 nonoverlapping, connected, edge-sharing district polygons cover the main districtable urban body with explicit purposeful internal open-space reservations, not the countryside. Walls are independent physical works, not district boundaries by definition. Published City district identities, types and edges remain final at Street fidelity; no new people, built capital or historical years.
items.Observable effects: A stylized but causally legible city of contrasting districts whose forms strongly embody their types even without labels: where warranted, crowded poorly maintained warrens, spacious high-investment residential grounds, market corridors, sacred precincts, monumental administrative seats, guarded compounds, workshops and distinct culture/template-conditioned districts. City stencil remains a strong dense/urbanizing influence on its interior; outside it may be farms, road-linked suburbs, hamlets or works without being assigned districts. These are example realizations, not mandatory every-city archetype quotas.
items.Other process interactions: City template policy supplies eligible district types and spatial/tenure/axis patterns. Early town.districts district programs actively propose strong spatial claims, demand and morphological obligations BEFORE and DURING land competition, collective investment, construction and movement. Those processes can reinforce, modify or defeat district proposals via real economic/physical feedback. District process finally resolves programs and boundaries by constrained space filling with voids; classification/publication only serializes/labels the ALREADY GENERATED types/geometry.
items.Responsibility / phenomenon: At City fidelity, generate strongly differentiated, causally supported district types under the selected settlement template, let those districts compete to shape real construction, major circulation, investments and rights, then resolve their authoritative permanent space-filling polygons with purposeful voids. Districts are generative urban entities and embodiments of their type, NOT a derived classification, naming pass or GIS-only publication concern.
items.Review notes: Owner correction: Do NOT demote town.districts to ClassificationPublication. This is a full Semantic process with early generative district identity/type and late permanent polygon partition. Restore the City stencil as a strong internal built-intensity/urban-form prior with a permeable edge; the prior must not eliminate surrounding farms, road stops, scattered development or satellites. The setting deliberately amplifies legibility of characteristic district types beyond bland realistic averages, while keeping them grounded in cause.
items.Semantic name: Generative district identities, morphology and permanent partition
items.Shared questions / coupling: The selected City founding template supplies a palette of eligible district programs and city-wide rules, NOT a finished layout. Every district program exposes its meaningful construction pressure, openness/intensity, preferred access, enclosure/tenure and civic/economic demands as typed inputs to movement, construction, land competition and collective investment. Feedback from those owners changes viability and shape. District type is authoritative generated state, not a post-hoc derived label.
items.Spatial & temporal scope: City: first generate competing district programs influenced by the strong city stencil, then co-evolve their spatial consequences with other City processes, then fix final authoritative district polygons and identities. Non-core suburbs/roadside/rural sites outside stencil remain allowed but generally undistricted. Street: inherit final type, boundaries, reserved ground and corresponding finer template guidance; reveal local streets and structures without reclassifying/repartitioning districts. World/Region have no City district geometry.
